coordinate, there are `C` and `0 ≤ ρ < 1` with `d_TV(Pⁿ(x, ·), π) ≤ C ρⁿ` for every start `x`.

articles.title: The Metropolis–Hastings chain converges to its target
articles.statement:
Under the hypotheses of
`isPrimitive_mhMatrix`, there are `C` and `0 ≤ ρ < 1` with `d_TV(Pⁿ(x, ·), π) ≤ C ρⁿ` for every
start `x`.

articles.title: Detailed balance for a Gibbs update
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the
configurations $x : \iota \to S$, with $\iota$ and $S$ finite, such that $\pi(x) \neq 0$ for every
$x$, and for a coordinate $i$ let $P_i(x, y)$ be the probability that the Gibbs update of
coordinate $i$ moves $x$ to $y$. Then $\pi(x) P_i(x, y) = \pi(y) P_i(y, x)$ for all
configurations $x$ and $y$.

When $x$ and $y$ differ at most in coordinate $i$, both sides equal $\pi(x) \pi(y) / Z$ for the
same normalizer $Z$; otherwise both sides are $0$.

articles.title: Gibbs update
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the configurations
$x : \iota \to S$, with $\iota$ and $S$ finite, such that $\pi(x) \neq 0$ for every $x$. The Gibbs
update of coordinate $i \in \iota$ from $x$ is the probability distribution of $x[i \mapsto s]$,
the configuration $x$ with coordinate $i$ set to $s$, where $s$ is drawn from the conditional law
of coordinate $i$ given the other coordinates of $x$.

articles.title: First step of a Gibbs sweep
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the configurations
$x : \iota \to S$, with $\iota$ and $S$ finite, such that $\pi(x) \neq 0$ for every $x$. For a list
$l$ of coordinates let $K_l$ be the systematic-scan Gibbs sampler for $l$, and for a coordinate $i$
let $P_i$ be the Markov kernel of the Gibbs update of coordinate $i$. Then for every configuration
$x$, the law $K_{(i, l)}(x)$ of the sampler for the list $(i, l)$ obtained by putting $i$ in front
of $l$ is the mixture $\int K_l(y) \, P_i(x, dy)$: first coordinate $i$ is updated, then the sweep
$l$ runs from the result.

articles.title: Gibbs sweep matrix is stochastic
articles.statement: The Gibbs sweep matrix is stochastic.

articles.title: Positivity of Gibbs sweep transition probabilities
articles.statement:
If the sweep visits every coordinate, every transition probability of the sweep is
positive.

articles.title: Transition matrix of the systematic-scan Gibbs sweep
articles.statement:
The transition matrix `P(x, y) = gibbsSweep π hπ l x {y}` of the systematic-scan Gibbs
sweep along `l`, as a real matrix.

articles.title: Systematic-scan Gibbs sampler
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the
configurations $x : \iota \to S$, with $\iota$ and $S$ finite, such that $\pi(x) \neq 0$ for every
$x$. For a list $l = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of coordinates, the systematic-scan Gibbs sampler is the
Markov kernel on configurations that applies the Gibbs updates of the coordinates
$i_1, i_2, \dots, i_n$ in this order; for the empty list it is the identity kernel.

articles.title: Gibbs sampling leaves the target stationary
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on
the configurations $x : \iota \to S$, with $\iota$ and $S$ finite, such that $\pi(x) \neq 0$ for
every $x$. For every coordinate $i$, $\pi$ is an invariant measure of the Markov kernel of the
Gibbs update of coordinate $i$: if $x$ is drawn from $\pi$ and coordinate $i$ is resampled from
its conditional law given the other coordinates, the result is again distributed as $\pi$.

articles.title: A full Gibbs sweep leaves the target stationary
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on
the configurations $x : \iota \to S$, with $\iota$ and $S$ finite, such that $\pi(x) \neq 0$ for
every $x$. For every finite list $l$ of coordinates, in any order and possibly with repetitions,
$\pi$ is an invariant measure of the systematic-scan Gibbs sampler that updates the coordinates in
the order of $l$.

articles.title: The target is stationary for Metropolis–Hastings
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite state space
with a measurable structure in which singletons are measurable, $\pi$ a probability distribution
on $\alpha$ and $Q$ a proposal assigning to each $x \in \alpha$ a probability distribution
$Q(x, \cdot)$ on $\alpha$. Then $\pi$, viewed as a measure, is invariant for the Markov kernel
$\kappa$ of the Metropolis–Hastings step for target $\pi$ and proposal $Q$: for every measurable
set $B$, $\int \kappa(x, B) \, d\pi(x) = \pi(B)$.

No positivity or symmetry assumption on $\pi$ or $Q$ is needed.

articles.title: Detailed balance implies invariance
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite state space with a measurable
structure in which singletons are measurable, $\pi$ a probability distribution on $\alpha$ and $P$
a transition rule assigning to each $x \in \alpha$ a probability distribution $P(x, \cdot)$ on
$\alpha$. If $\pi(x) P(x, y) = \pi(y) P(y, x)$ for all $x, y \in \alpha$, then $\pi$, viewed as a
measure, is invariant for the Markov kernel $\kappa$ of $P$: for every measurable set $B$,
$\int \kappa(x, B) \, d\pi(x) = \pi(B)$.

articles.title: Primitivity of the Metropolis–Hastings matrix
articles.statement:
For a target with full support and a proposal with primitive transition matrix and symmetric
support, the Metropolis–Hastings matrix is primitive.

articles.title: Gibbs updates are reversible
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the
configurations $x : \iota \to S$, with $\iota$ and $S$ finite, such that $\pi(x) \neq 0$ for every
$x$. For every coordinate $i$, the Markov kernel $K$ of the Gibbs update of coordinate $i$ is
reversible with respect to $\pi$: for all measurable sets $A$ and $B$ of configurations,
$\int_A K(x, B) \, d\pi(x) = \int_B K(x, A) \, d\pi(x)$.

articles.title: The Metropolis–Hastings kernel is reversible
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite state space with a
measurable structure in which singletons are measurable, $\pi$ a probability distribution on
$\alpha$ and $Q$ a proposal assigning to each $x \in \alpha$ a probability distribution
$Q(x, \cdot)$ on $\alpha$. Then the Markov kernel $\kappa$ of the Metropolis–Hastings step for
target $\pi$ and proposal $Q$ is reversible with respect to $\pi$, viewed as a measure: for all
measurable sets $A$ and $B$, $\int_A \kappa(x, B) \, d\pi(x) = \int_B \kappa(x, A) \, d\pi(x)$.

articles.title: Detailed balance implies reversibility
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite state space with a
measurable structure in which singletons are measurable, $\pi$ a probability distribution on
$\alpha$ and $P$ a transition rule assigning to each $x \in \alpha$ a probability distribution
$P(x, \cdot)$ on $\alpha$. If $\pi(x) P(x, y) = \pi(y) P(y, x)$ for all $x, y \in \alpha$, then
the Markov kernel $\kappa$ of $P$ is reversible with respect to $\pi$, viewed as a measure: for
all measurable sets $A$ and $B$,
$\int_A \kappa(x, B) \, d\pi(x) = \int_B \kappa(x, A) \, d\pi(x)$.

articles.title: Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability
articles.statement:
For a probability distribution $\pi$ on
$\alpha$ and a proposal $Q$ assigning to each $x \in \alpha$ a probability distribution
$Q(x, \cdot)$ on $\alpha$, the acceptance probability of a move from $x$ to $y$ is
$a(x, y) = \min\bigl(1, \pi(y) Q(y, x) / (\pi(x) Q(x, y))\bigr)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$
with $c / 0 = \infty$ for $c \ne 0$ and $0 / 0 = 0$.

articles.title: Detailed balance for Metropolis–Hastings
articles.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on a
type $\alpha$, $Q$ a proposal assigning to each $x \in \alpha$ a probability distribution
$Q(x, \cdot)$ on $\alpha$, and $P(x, y)$ the probability that one Metropolis–Hastings step for
target $\pi$ and proposal $Q$ moves from $x$ to $y$. Then $\pi(x) P(x, y) = \pi(y) P(y, x)$ for
all $x, y \in \alpha$.

For $x \ne y$ both sides equal $\min(\pi(x) Q(x, y), \pi(y) Q(y, x))$; no positivity or symmetry
assumption on $\pi$ or $Q$ is needed.

articles.title: Metropolis–Hastings matrix is stochastic
articles.statement: The Metropolis–Hastings matrix is stochastic.

articles.title: Metropolis–Hastings transition matrix
articles.statement:
The transition matrix `P(x, y) = mhStep π Q x y` of the Metropolis–Hastings chain, as a real
matrix.

articles.title: Metropolis–Hastings step
articles.statement:
For a probability distribution $\pi$ on $\alpha$ (the target)
and a proposal $Q$ assigning to each $x \in \alpha$ a probability distribution $Q(x, \cdot)$ on
$\alpha$, one Metropolis–Hastings step from $x$ is the distribution of the following move: draw
$y$ from $Q(x, \cdot)$, then move to $y$ with the Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability
$a(x, y)$, and otherwise stay at $x$.

articles.title: Markov kernel of a transition rule
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite state space with a measurable
structure in which singletons are measurable. A transition rule $P$ assigning to each $x \in \alpha$
a probability distribution $P(x, \cdot)$ on $\alpha$ gives the Markov kernel on $\alpha$ that sends
$x$ to $P(x, \cdot)$ viewed as a probability measure, so a set $B$ gets mass
$\sum_{y \in B} P(x, y)$.

articles.title: Probabilities of a finite law sum to one
articles.statement: The probabilities of a law on a finite type, as reals, sum to `1`.

articles.title: Symmetry of differing in one coordinate
articles.statement:
For functions $x, y : \iota \to S$ and a coordinate
$i \in \iota$, if setting coordinate $i$ of $x$ to $y(i)$ gives $y$, then setting coordinate $i$ of
$y$ to $x(i)$ gives $x$.

articles.title: Target is stationary for the Gibbs sweep matrix
articles.statement: The target is stationary for the Gibbs sweep matrix.

articles.title: Target is stationary for the Metropolis–Hastings matrix
articles.statement: The target is stationary for the Metropolis–Hastings matrix.

articles.title: Mean-field (CAVI) update of the second factor
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets, let
$p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a joint and let $q_1 : A \to \mathbb{R}$. The
coordinate-ascent update of the second factor is the function $q_2 : B \to \mathbb{R}$ given by

$$q_2(b) = \frac{\exp F(b)}{\sum_{b' \in B} \exp F(b')},$$

where $F(b) = \sum_{a \in A} q_1(a) \log p(a, b)$. That is,
$q_2(b) \propto \exp \mathbb{E}_{q_1}[\log p(\cdot, b)]$; it is the update of the first factor
applied to the joint with its two factors swapped.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm extended by $\log x = \log |x|$ for $x < 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: Mean-field (CAVI) update of the first factor
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets, let
$p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a joint and let $q_2 : B \to \mathbb{R}$. The
coordinate-ascent update of the first factor is the function $q_1 : A \to \mathbb{R}$ given by

$$q_1(a) = \frac{\exp E(a)}{\sum_{a' \in A} \exp E(a')},$$

where $E(a) = \sum_{b \in B} q_2(b) \log p(a, b)$ is the expected log-joint of $a$ under $q_2$.
That is, $q_1(a) \propto \exp \mathbb{E}_{q_2}[\log p(a, \cdot)]$.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm extended by $\log x = \log |x|$ for $x < 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: The ELBO is the log evidence minus the KL divergence
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a nonempty finite set
and let $p : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ give the joint values $p(z) = p(x, z)$ of a fixed observation $x$
with each latent value $z \in Z$, where $p(z) > 0$ for every $z \in Z$. Let
$p(x) = \sum_{z \in Z} p(z)$ be the evidence and $p(z \mid x) = p(z) / p(x)$ the posterior. For
$q, r : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ write
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z \in Z} q(z) \bigl(\log p(z) - \log q(z)\bigr)$ and
$\mathrm{KL}(q \,\|\, r) = \sum_{z \in Z} q(z) \bigl(\log q(z) - \log r(z)\bigr)$. Then for every
probability distribution $q$ on $Z$,
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \log p(x) - \mathrm{KL}\bigl(q \,\|\, p(\cdot \mid x)\bigr)$.

articles.title: Mean-field coordinate ascent never decreases the ELBO
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty finite
sets, let $p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a joint, and let $q_1^{(0)}$ and $q_2^{(0)}$ be
probability distributions on $A$ and $B$. A sweep of coordinate ascent replaces $q_1$ by its CAVI
update $q_1'(a) \propto \exp \sum_{b} q_2(b) \log p(a, b)$ and then $q_2$ by its CAVI update
$q_2'(b) \propto \exp \sum_{a} q_1'(a) \log p(a, b)$, each normalized to sum to $1$. Let
$(q_1^{(t)}, q_2^{(t)})$ be the result of $t$ sweeps from $(q_1^{(0)}, q_2^{(0)})$. Then
$t \mapsto \mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1^{(t)} q_2^{(t)})$ is monotone on $\mathbb{N}$, where
$(q_1 q_2)(a, b) = q_1(a) q_2(b)$ and
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z} q(z) (\log p(z) - \log q(z))$.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm extended by $\log x = \log |x|$ for $x < 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: The CAVI update of the second factor does not decrease the ELBO
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite
sets with $B$ nonempty, let $p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a joint, and let $q_1$ and $q_2$ be
probability distributions on $A$ and $B$. Let $q_2^*$ be the CAVI update of the second factor
given $q_1$, $q_2^*(b) = \exp F(b) / \sum_{b' \in B} \exp F(b')$ with
$F(b) = \sum_{a \in A} q_1(a) \log p(a, b)$. Then
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1 q_2) \le \mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1 q_2^*)$, where
$(q_1 q_2)(a, b) = q_1(a) q_2(b)$ and
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z} q(z) (\log p(z) - \log q(z))$.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm extended by $\log x = \log |x|$ for $x < 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: The CAVI update maximizes the ELBO over the first factor
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets
with $A$ nonempty, let $p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a joint, and let $q_1$ and $q_2$ be
probability distributions on $A$ and $B$. Let $q_1^*$ be the CAVI update of the first factor
given $q_2$, $q_1^*(a) = \exp E(a) / \sum_{a' \in A} \exp E(a')$ with
$E(a) = \sum_{b \in B} q_2(b) \log p(a, b)$. Then
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1 q_2) \le \mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1^* q_2)$, where
$(q_1 q_2)(a, b) = q_1(a) q_2(b)$ and
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z} q(z) (\log p(z) - \log q(z))$.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm extended by $\log x = \log |x|$ for $x < 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: A sweep of coordinate ascent does not decrease the ELBO
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty
finite sets, let $p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a joint, and let $q_1$ and $q_2$ be probability
distributions on $A$ and $B$. One sweep replaces $q_1$ by its CAVI update $q_1'$ given $q_2$ and
then $q_2$ by its CAVI update $q_2'$ given $q_1'$, where
$q_1'(a) \propto \exp \sum_{b} q_2(b) \log p(a, b)$ and
$q_2'(b) \propto \exp \sum_{a} q_1'(a) \log p(a, b)$, each normalized to sum to $1$. Then
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1 q_2) \le \mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1' q_2')$, where
$(q_1 q_2)(a, b) = q_1(a) q_2(b)$ and
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z} q(z) (\log p(z) - \log q(z))$.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm extended by $\log x = \log |x|$ for $x < 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: The ELBO is a lower bound
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a finite set and let $p : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
$p(z) > 0$ for all $z$, with evidence $p(x) = \sum_{z \in Z} p(z)$. Then for every probability
distribution $q$ on $Z$,

$$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z \in Z} q(z) (\log p(z) - \log q(z)) \le \log p(x).$$

This is Gibbs' inequality.

articles.title: The ELBO bound is attained at the posterior
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a nonempty finite set and let
$p : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $p(z) > 0$ for all $z$, with evidence $p(x) = \sum_{z \in Z} p(z)$
and posterior $p(z \mid x) = p(z) / p(x)$. Then $\mathrm{ELBO}(p, p(\cdot \mid x)) = \log p(x)$,
where $\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z} q(z) (\log p(z) - \log q(z))$.

articles.title: ELBO of a product distribution
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets, let
$p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$ be a joint, and let $q_1$ and $q_2$ be probability distributions
on $A$ and $B$, with product $(q_1 q_2)(a, b) = q_1(a) q_2(b)$. Then

$$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q_1 q_2) = \sum_{a \in A} q_1(a) \bigl(E(a) - \log q_1(a)\bigr) -
\sum_{b \in B} q_2(b) \log q_2(b),$$

where $E(a) = \sum_{b \in B} q_2(b) \log p(a, b)$ is the expected log-joint of $a$ under $q_2$
and $\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z} q(z) (\log p(z) - \log q(z))$. So the ELBO splits into a
$q_1$-term and the entropy of $q_2$.

Here $\log$ is the real logarithm extended by $\log x = \log |x|$ for $x < 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$.

articles.title: Evidence lower bound of a single observation
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a finite set, let
$p : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ give the joint values $p(z) = p(x, z)$ of a fixed observation $x$ with each
latent value $z \in Z$, and let $q : Z \to \mathbb{R}$. The evidence lower bound of $q$ is
$\mathrm{ELBO}(p, q) = \sum_{z \in Z} q(z) \bigl(\log p(z) - \log q(z)\bigr)$.

articles.title: The EM evidence lower bound is a sum of per-point ELBOs
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a finite set, let
$p_\theta(x, z)$ be real numbers indexed by parameters $\theta$, observations $x$ and latent values
$z \in Z$, let $x_1, \dots, x_N$ be data, let $\theta$ be a parameter and let
$q_1, \dots, q_N : Z \to \mathbb{R}$. Then the evidence lower bound of expectation-maximization,
$\sum_{n=1}^N \sum_{z \in Z} q_n(z) \bigl(\log p_\theta(x_n, z) - \log q_n(z)\bigr)$, equals
$\sum_{n=1}^N \mathrm{ELBO}(p_\theta(x_n, \cdot), q_n)$, the sum over the data points of the
single-observation evidence lower bound of $q_n$ for the joint values
$z \mapsto p_\theta(x_n, z)$.

articles.title: Evidence of an unnormalized posterior
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a finite set and let
$p : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ give the joint values $p(z) = p(x, z)$ of a fixed observation $x$ with each
latent value $z \in Z$ (an unnormalized posterior). The evidence is
$p(x) = \sum_{z \in Z} p(z)$.

articles.title: Expected log-joint
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets and let $p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$
and $q_2 : B \to \mathbb{R}$. For $a \in A$, the expected log-joint of $a$ under $q_2$ is
$\mathbb{E}_{q_2}[\log p(a, \cdot)] = \sum_{b \in B} q_2(b) \log p(a, b)$.

articles.title: Gibbs' inequality
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a finite set, let $q$ be a probability distribution on $Z$,
and let $r : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $r(z) > 0$ for every $z \in Z$ and
$\sum_{z \in Z} r(z) = 1$. Then
$\mathrm{KL}(q \,\|\, r) = \sum_{z \in Z} q(z) \bigl(\log q(z) - \log r(z)\bigr) \ge 0$.

articles.title: The KL divergence to the posterior is nonnegative
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a nonempty finite set, let
$p : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $p(z) > 0$ for every $z \in Z$, and let $q$ be a probability
distribution on $Z$. Let $\pi(z) = p(z) / \sum_{z' \in Z} p(z')$ be the posterior of $p$. Then
$\mathrm{KL}(q \,\|\, \pi) = \sum_{z \in Z} q(z) \bigl(\log q(z) - \log \pi(z)\bigr) \ge 0$.

articles.title: Finite Kullback–Leibler formula
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a finite set and let $q, r : Z \to \mathbb{R}$.
The Kullback–Leibler formula of $q$ against $r$ is
$\mathrm{KL}(q \,\|\, r) = \sum_{z \in Z} q(z) \bigl(\log q(z) - \log r(z)\bigr)$; terms with
$q(z) = 0$ vanish.

This is the Kullback–Leibler divergence of $q$ from $r$ when $r(z) > 0$ for every $z$, the only
case used here (where $r$ is the posterior of a positive joint). If $r$ vanishes where $q$ does
not, the divergence is infinite, but this real-valued formula is finite, since it reads $\log 0$
as $0$.

articles.title: Posterior of an unnormalized joint
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be a finite set and let
$p : Z \to \mathbb{R}$ give the joint values $p(z) = p(x, z)$ of a fixed observation $x$ with each
latent value $z \in Z$. The posterior of $z$ is $p(z \mid x) = p(z) / p(x)$, where
$p(x) = \sum_{z' \in Z} p(z')$ is the evidence (the quotient is read as $0$ when $p(x) = 0$).

articles.title: Mean-field product distribution
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets and let
$q_1 : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and $q_2 : B \to \mathbb{R}$. Their mean-field (product) distribution is
the function on $A \times B$ given by $q(a, b) = q_1(a) \, q_2(b)$.

articles.title: Swapped joint
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets and let $p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$. The
swapped joint of $p$ is the function on $B \times A$ given by $(b, a) \mapsto p(a, b)$.

articles.title: Mean-field coordinate-ascent sweep
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets and
$p : A \times B \to \mathbb{R}$. One sweep of coordinate ascent (CAVI) sends a pair of factors
$(q_1, q_2)$, with $q_1 : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and $q_2 : B \to \mathbb{R}$, to $(q_1', q_2')$, where
$q_1'$ is the CAVI update of the first factor given $q_2$,
$q_1'(a) = \exp(\sum_b q_2(b) \log p(a, b)) / \sum_{a'} \exp(\sum_b q_2(b) \log p(a', b))$, and
$q_2'$ is the CAVI update of the second factor given the new first factor $q_1'$,
$q_2'(b) = \exp(\sum_a q_1'(a) \log p(a, b)) / \sum_{b'} \exp(\sum_a q_1'(a) \log p(a, b'))$.
The old first factor $q_1$ is not used.

Here $\log x$ means $\log |x|$ for $x \ne 0$ and $\log 0 = 0$, so $p$ need not be positive.

articles.title: Product Bernoulli probability mass function
articles.statement:
For a vector $p \in \mathbb{R}^d$ of success
probabilities and a binary vector $x \in \{0, 1\}^d$, the probability of $x$ under the product of
$d$ independent Bernoulli distributions with parameters $p_1, \dots, p_d$ is

$$\prod_{j=1}^{d} p_j^{x_j} (1 - p_j)^{1 - x_j},$$

that is, the product over $j$ of $p_j$ when $x_j = 1$ and of $1 - p_j$ when $x_j = 0$.

articles.title: Component term of the EM objective for full-covariance Gaussian mixtures
articles.statement:
Given points
$x_1, \dots, x_N$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ of a $K$-component
full-covariance Gaussian mixture, a component $k$, a mean $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real
$d \times d$ matrix $S$, the component term is

$$
C_k(\mu, S) = \sum_n r_{nk} \log \mathcal{N}(x_n \mid \mu, S),
$$

where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$ and
$\mathcal{N}(\cdot \mid \mu, S)$ is the multivariate Gaussian density with mean $\mu$ and
covariance matrix $S$.

The matrix $S$ is not required to be positive definite; the density is defined for every real
matrix.

articles.title: The mean and covariance updates maximize each component term
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data in general position (at least one point, and not all
in an affine hyperplane), let $\theta$ be valid mixture parameters with responsibilities
$r_{nk}$, and fix a component $k$. Write $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, S)$ for the multivariate
Gaussian density and let $\mu'_k$ and $\Sigma'_k$ be the responsibility-weighted mean and the
responsibility-weighted sample covariance of the data for component $k$. Then for every
$\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and every positive definite $d \times d$ matrix $S$,

$$\sum_n r_{nk} \log \mathcal{N}(x_n \mid \mu, S) \le
\sum_n r_{nk} \log \mathcal{N}(x_n \mid \mu'_k, \Sigma'_k).$$

articles.title: The mean and variance updates maximize each component term
articles.statement:
Let $x_1, \dots, x_N$ be
points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that are not all equal, let $\theta$ be valid parameters of a
$K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture, let $k$ be a component, and let $r_{nk}$ be the
responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$. For every $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and
every real $v > 0$, the component term

$$
C_k(\mu, v) = \sum_n r_{nk} \bigl(-\tfrac{d}{2} \log(2\pi v) - \|x_n - \mu\|^2 / (2v)\bigr)
$$

satisfies $C_k(\mu, v) \le C_k(\mu_k', v_k')$, where $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$,
$\mu_k' = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$ is the responsibility-weighted mean,
$S_k = \sum_n r_{nk} \|x_n - \mu_k'\|^2$ and $v_k' = S_k / (d N_k)$.

articles.title: Component term of the EM objective for isotropic Gaussian mixtures
articles.statement:
Given points
$x_1, \dots, x_N$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ of a $K$-component isotropic
Gaussian mixture, a component $k$, a mean $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $v$, the
component term is

$$
C_k(\mu, v) = \sum_n r_{nk} \bigl(-\tfrac{d}{2} \log(2\pi v) - \|x_n - \mu\|^2 / (2v)\bigr),
$$

where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$.

For $v > 0$ this is $\sum_n r_{nk} \log \mathcal{N}(x_n \mid \mu, v I)$, where
$\mathcal{N}(\cdot \mid \mu, v I)$ is the isotropic Gaussian density with mean $\mu$ and
covariance $v I$.

articles.title: The EM objective of an isotropic Gaussian mixture splits by component
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N$ be points of $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $\theta'$ and $\theta$ be valid parameters
of a $K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture, where $\theta'$ has weights $\pi_k'$, means
$\mu_k'$ and variances $v_k'$. Then the EM objective of the mixture's joint density satisfies

$$
Q(\theta' \mid \theta) = \sum_k \bigl(N_k \log \pi_k' + C_k(\mu_k', v_k')\bigr),
$$

where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$,
$N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$ and
$C_k(\mu, v) = \sum_n r_{nk} \bigl(-\tfrac{d}{2} \log(2\pi v) - \|x_n - \mu\|^2 / (2v)\bigr)$.

articles.title: The EM objective of a full-covariance Gaussian mixture splits by component
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N$ be points of $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $\theta'$ and $\theta$ be valid parameters
of a $K$-component full-covariance Gaussian mixture, where $\theta'$ has weights $\pi_k'$, means
$\mu_k'$ and covariance matrices $\Sigma_k'$. Then the EM objective of the mixture's joint density
satisfies

$$
Q(\theta' \mid \theta) = \sum_k \bigl(N_k \log \pi_k' + C_k(\mu_k', \Sigma_k')\bigr),
$$

where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$,
$N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$ and $C_k(\mu, S) = \sum_n r_{nk} \log \mathcal{N}(x_n \mid \mu, S)$, with
$\mathcal{N}(\cdot \mid \mu, S)$ the multivariate Gaussian density with mean $\mu$ and covariance
matrix $S$.

articles.title: Decomposition of the EM objective for the Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$ be data and let $\theta$ and $\theta'$ be valid parameters of a
mixture of $K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions (positive mixing weights summing to one and
success probabilities in $(0, 1)$), where $\theta'$ has mixing weights $\pi'_k$ and success
probabilities $p'_{kj}$. Write $p_\theta(x, k)$ for the joint probability of $x$ and component $k$
under $\theta$ (the mixing weight of $k$ times the product Bernoulli probability of $x$),
$r_{nk} = p_\theta(k \mid x_n) = p_\theta(x_n, k) / \sum_l p_\theta(x_n, l)$ for the posterior
probability of component $k$ given $x_n$, $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, and $A_{kj}$ and $B_{kj}$ for the
sums of $r_{nk}$ over the points $x_n$ whose $j$-th coordinate $x_{nj}$ is $1$ and is $0$
respectively. Then the EM objective
$Q(\theta' \mid \theta) = \sum_n \sum_k r_{nk} \log p_{\theta'}(x_n, k)$ equals

$$\sum_{k=1}^{K} \Big( N_k \log \pi'_k + \sum_{j=1}^{d} \big( A_{kj} \log p'_{kj} +
B_{kj} \log (1 - p'_{kj}) \big) \Big).$$

The first term depends only on the mixing weights and each remaining term on a single $p'_{kj}$.

articles.title: The M-step for isotropic Gaussian mixtures maximizes the EM objective
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N$ be points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that are not all equal, let $\theta$ be valid
parameters of a $K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture, and let $\theta^+$ be the result of
the EM step applied to $\theta$. Then every valid parameter $\theta'$ satisfies
$Q(\theta' \mid \theta) \le Q(\theta^+ \mid \theta)$, where $Q$ is the EM objective of the
mixture's joint density.

articles.title: The M-step of the full-covariance Gaussian mixture maximizes the EM objective
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data in general position: $N > 0$, and for every nonzero
$v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ the values $\langle v, x_n \rangle$ are not all equal. Let $\theta$ be valid
parameters of a $K$-component full-covariance Gaussian mixture, and let $\theta^+$ be the result
of the EM step applied to $\theta$. Then every valid parameter $\theta'$ satisfies
$Q(\theta' \mid \theta) \le Q(\theta^+ \mid \theta)$, where $Q$ is the EM objective of the
mixture's joint density.

articles.title: The M-step of the Bernoulli mixture maximizes the EM objective
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$ be rich data: $N > 0$, and for every coordinate $j < d$ some
$x_n$ has $j$-th coordinate $1$ and some $x_m$ has $j$-th coordinate $0$. Let $\theta$ be valid
parameters of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions, and let $\theta^+$ be the
result of the EM step applied to $\theta$. Then every valid parameter $\theta'$ satisfies
$Q(\theta' \mid \theta) \le Q(\theta^+ \mid \theta)$, where $Q$ is the EM objective of the
mixture's joint distribution.

articles.title: The EM step for isotropic Gaussian mixtures
articles.statement:
Let $x_1, \dots, x_N$ be points of
$\mathbb{R}^d$ that are not all equal and let $\theta$ be valid parameters of a $K$-component
isotropic Gaussian mixture. With $r_{nk}$ the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under
$\theta$ (the E-step), the EM step sends $\theta$ to the valid parameters with weights
$\pi_k' = N_k / N$, means $\mu_k' = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$ and variances
$v_k' = S_k / (d N_k)$, where $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$ and $S_k = \sum_n r_{nk} \|x_n - \mu_k'\|^2$
(the M-step).

articles.title: EM step for the full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
For data
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ in general position (at least one point, and not all in an
affine hyperplane) and valid parameters $\theta$, the EM step returns the M-step parameters of
$\theta$: with responsibilities $r_{nk}$ under $\theta$ and $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, the new
weights are $N_k / N$, the new means are the responsibility-weighted means and the new
covariances are the responsibility-weighted sample covariances. General position makes these
parameters valid.

articles.title: One EM step for the Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$ be data with
$N \ge 1$ in which every coordinate takes both values. For valid parameters $\theta$ of a mixture
of $K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions, the EM step maps $\theta$ to the parameters with
mixing weights $\pi'_k = N_k / N$ and success probabilities $p'_{kj} = A_{kj} / N_k$, where
$r_{nk}$ is the posterior probability of component $k$ given $x_n$ under $\theta$,
$N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, and $A_{kj}$ is the sum of $r_{nk}$ over the points with $x_{nj} = 1$. On
such data these parameters are again valid.

articles.title: Isotropic Gaussian density
articles.statement:
For a mean $\mu \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a variance $v \ge 0$,
the isotropic Gaussian density at $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is
$\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, v I) = \prod_{i=1}^{d} \varphi_{\mu_i, v}(x_i)$, where
$\varphi_{m, v}$ is the one-dimensional Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$.

For $v = 0$ the one-dimensional density is identically $0$, following Mathlib's convention.

articles.title: Joint density of an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
For valid parameters $\theta$ of a
$K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture in $\mathbb{R}^d$, with weights $\pi_k$, means $\mu_k$
and variances $\sigma_k^2$, the joint density of a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a component $k$
is $p_\theta(x, k) = \pi_k \, \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu_k, \sigma_k^2 I)$, where
$\mathcal{N}(\cdot \mid \mu, v I)$ is the isotropic Gaussian density.

articles.title: Joint density of the full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
For valid parameters $\theta$ with
weights $\pi_k$, means $\mu_k$ and covariances $\Sigma_k$, the joint density of a point
$x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a component $k$ is
$p_\theta(x, k) = \pi_k \, \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu_k, \Sigma_k)$, where
$\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, \Sigma)$ is the multivariate Gaussian density.

articles.title: Joint distribution of the Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
For valid parameters $\theta$ of a mixture of
$K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions, with mixing weights $\pi_k$ and success probabilities
$p_{kj}$, the joint probability of a binary vector $x \in \{0, 1\}^d$ and a component $k$ is

$$p_\theta(x, k) = \pi_k \prod_{j=1}^{d} p_{kj}^{x_j} (1 - p_{kj})^{1 - x_j},$$

that is, $\pi_k$ times the product Bernoulli probability of $x$ with parameters
$p_{k1}, \dots, p_{kd}$.

articles.title: Log-density of the isotropic Gaussian
articles.statement:
For $\mu, x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a variance
$v > 0$, the isotropic Gaussian density $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, v I)$ with mean $\mu$ and
covariance $v I$ satisfies
$\log \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, v I) = -\tfrac{d}{2} \log(2 \pi v) - \|x - \mu\|^2 / (2 v)$.

articles.title: The log-likelihood is monotone along the EM iterates of an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Let $x_1, \dots, x_N$ be points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that are not all equal, let $\theta_0$ be valid
parameters of a $K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture, and let $\theta_t$ be the result of $t$
EM steps from $\theta_0$. Then $\ell(\theta_t)$ is nondecreasing in $t \in \mathbb{N}$, where
$\ell$ is the log-likelihood of the data under the mixture.

articles.title: The log-likelihood is monotone along the EM iterates of a full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
**The log-likelihood is monotone along the EM iterates of a full-covariance Gaussian
mixture.** Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data in general position: $N > 0$, and for
every nonzero $v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ the values $\langle v, x_n \rangle$ are not all equal. Let
$\theta_0$ be valid parameters of a $K$-component full-covariance Gaussian mixture, and let
$\theta_t$ be the result of $t$ EM steps from $\theta_0$. Then $\ell(\theta_t)$ is nondecreasing
in $t \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\ell$ is the log-likelihood of the data under the mixture's joint
density.

articles.title: The log-likelihood is monotone along the EM iterates of a Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$ be rich data: $N > 0$, and for every coordinate $j < d$ some
$x_n$ has $j$-th coordinate $1$ and some $x_m$ has $j$-th coordinate $0$. Let $\theta_0$ be valid
parameters of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions, and let $\theta_t$ be the
result of $t$ EM steps from $\theta_0$. Then $\ell(\theta_t)$ is nondecreasing in
$t \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\ell$ is the log-likelihood of the data under the mixture's joint
distribution.

articles.title: Each EM step for the Gaussian mixture does not decrease the log-likelihood
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N$ be points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that are not all equal and let $\theta$ be valid
parameters of a $K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture. Then $\ell(\theta) \le \ell(\theta^+)$,
where $\ell$ is the log-likelihood of the data under the mixture and $\theta^+$ is the result of
the EM step applied to $\theta$.

articles.title: Each EM step for the full-covariance Gaussian mixture does not decrease the log-likelihood
articles.statement:
**Each EM step for the full-covariance Gaussian mixture does not decrease the
log-likelihood.** Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be data in general position (at least
one point, and not all in an affine hyperplane) and let $\theta$ be valid parameters. If
$\theta^{+}$ is the result of one EM step from $\theta$, then $\ell(\theta) \le \ell(\theta^{+})$,
where $\ell$ is the log-likelihood of the data under the mixture.

articles.title: Each EM step for the Bernoulli mixture does not decrease the log-likelihood
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$ be rich data: $N > 0$, and for every coordinate $j < d$ some
$x_n$ has $j$-th coordinate $1$ and some $x_m$ has $j$-th coordinate $0$. Let $\theta$ be valid
parameters of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions. Then
$\ell(\theta) \le \ell(\theta^+)$, where $\ell$ is the log-likelihood of the data under the
mixture's joint distribution and $\theta^+$ is the result of the EM step applied to $\theta$.

articles.title: M-step of EM for an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Let $x_0, \dots, x_{N-1}$ be data
points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\theta$ be valid parameters of a $K$-component isotropic Gaussian
mixture, and let $r_{nk}$ be the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$. With
$N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, the M-step returns the parameters with mixing weights
$\pi_k' = N_k / N$, means $\mu_k' = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$ and variances
$\sigma_k'^2 = S_k / (d N_k)$, where $S_k = \sum_n r_{nk} \lVert x_n - \mu_k' \rVert^2$.

Division by zero is read as $0$.

articles.title: M-step of the full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
For data
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and valid parameters $\theta$ with responsibilities $r_{nk}$,
let $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$. The M-step parameters have weights $\pi'_k = N_k / N$, means
$\mu'_k = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$ and covariances
$\Sigma'_k = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} (x_n - \mu'_k)(x_n - \mu'_k)^{\top}$.

articles.title: The M-step of the Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
Let $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$ be data and
$\theta$ valid parameters of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions. With $r_{nk}$
the posterior probability of component $k$ given $x_n$ under $\theta$, $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$ and
$A_{kj} = \sum_n r_{nk} x_{nj}$, the M-step returns the parameters with mixing weights
$\pi'_k = N_k / N$ and success probabilities $p'_{kj} = A_{kj} / N_k$, where a quotient by $0$ is
read as $0$. These parameters need not be valid.

articles.title: Mixture density of an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
For valid parameters $\theta$ with
mixing weights $\pi_k$, means $\mu_k$ and variances $\sigma_k^2$, and every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$,
the marginal $p_\theta(x) = \sum_k p_\theta(x, k)$ of the joint density equals
$\sum_k \pi_k \, \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu_k, \sigma_k^2 I)$, where $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, v I)$
is the isotropic Gaussian density.

articles.title: Effective number of points in an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Given data points
$x_0, \dots, x_{N-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ of a $K$-component isotropic
Gaussian mixture and a component $k$, the effective number of points of $k$ is
$N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under
$\theta$, the posterior probability of $k$ given $x_n$.

articles.title: Effective number of points of a full-covariance mixture component
articles.statement:
For data
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and valid parameters $\theta$ with responsibilities $r_{nk}$,
the effective number of points of component $k$ is $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$.

articles.title: Effective number of points of a Bernoulli-mixture component
articles.statement:
For data
$x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$ and valid parameters $\theta$ of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$
Bernoulli distributions, the effective number of points of component $k$ is
$N_k = \sum_{n=1}^{N} r_{nk}$, where $r_{nk}$ is the posterior probability (responsibility) of
component $k$ given $x_n$ under $\theta$.

articles.title: The covariance update is positive definite
articles.statement:
Let $(x_n)_{n\lt N}$ be data in $\mathbb{R}^d$
in general position: $N > 0$, and for every nonzero $v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ the values
$\langle v, x_n \rangle$ are not all equal. Then for all valid parameters $\theta$ of the
$K$-component full-covariance Gaussian mixture and every component $k$, the covariance update
$\Sigma_k'$ (the responsibility-weighted sample covariance of the data about the
responsibility-weighted mean) is positive definite.

articles.title: Covariance update of the full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Given data $(x_n)_{n\lt N}$
in $\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ and a component $k$, let $r_{nk}$ be the
responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$, let $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, and let $\mu_k'$ be the
responsibility-weighted mean $N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$. The covariance update is the real
$d \times d$ matrix

$$\Sigma_k' = \frac{1}{N_k} \sum_n r_{nk} (x_n - \mu_k')(x_n - \mu_k')^{\top}.$$

When there are no data ($N = 0$), $N_k = 0$ and the convention $N_k^{-1} = 0$ makes
$\Sigma_k' = 0$.

articles.title: Mean update of the full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Given data $(x_n)_{n\lt N}$ in
$\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ and a component $k$, let $r_{nk}$ be the
responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ and let $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$. The mean update is the
responsibility-weighted mean

$$\mu_k' = \frac{1}{N_k} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n \in \mathbb{R}^d.$$

When there are no data ($N = 0$), $N_k = 0$ and the convention $N_k^{-1} = 0$ makes
$\mu_k' = 0$.

articles.title: M-step mean update for an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Given data points
$x_0, \dots, x_{N-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ of a $K$-component isotropic
Gaussian mixture and a component $k$, the updated mean of $k$ is the responsibility-weighted
mean $\mu_k' = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$, where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$
for $x_n$ under $\theta$ and $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$.

The inverse of $0$ is read as $0$.

articles.title: M-step variance update for an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Given data points
$x_0, \dots, x_{N-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ of a $K$-component isotropic
Gaussian mixture and a component $k$, the updated variance of $k$ is
$\sigma_k'^2 = S_k / (d N_k)$, where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$
under $\theta$, $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, $\mu_k' = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$ and
$S_k = \sum_n r_{nk} \lVert x_n - \mu_k' \rVert^2$.

Division by zero is read as $0$.

articles.title: Valid mixture parameters have at least one component
articles.statement:
If $\theta$ is a valid parameter of
a $K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions, then $K \ge 1$.

articles.title: Data that are not all equal
articles.statement:
A finite family of points $x_0, \dots, x_{N-1}$ in
$\mathbb{R}^d$ is not all equal when there are indices $n$ and $n'$ with $x_n \ne x_{n'}$.

articles.title: Responsibility-weighted count of ones
articles.statement:
For data $x_1, \dots, x_N \in \{0, 1\}^d$, valid
parameters $\theta$ of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions, a component $k$
and a coordinate $j$, this is the sum $\sum_{n \,:\, x_{nj} = 1} r_{nk}$, over the points whose
$j$-th coordinate is $1$, of the posterior probability $r_{nk}$ of component $k$ given $x_n$
under $\theta$.

articles.title: Parameters of an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Parameters of a $K$-component isotropic
Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions consist, for each component $k < K$, of a mixing weight
$\pi_k \in \mathbb{R}$, a mean $\mu_k \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a variance $\sigma_k^2 \ge 0$; component
$k$ has covariance $\sigma_k^2 I$.

No constraint is placed on the weights here; validity is a separate condition.

articles.title: Parameters of a full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
A parameter of the $K$-component
Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions with full covariances consists of, for each component
$k < K$, a real mixing weight $\pi_k$, a mean $\mu_k \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real $d \times d$
covariance matrix $\Sigma_k$, with no constraints imposed.

articles.title: Parameters of a Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
The parameters of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$
Bernoulli distributions are real mixing weights $\pi_k$ for $k < K$ and real success
probabilities $p_{kj}$ for every component $k < K$ and coordinate $j < d$. No constraint is
imposed on these numbers here; the admissible ones are the valid parameters.

articles.title: Responsibilities in an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
For valid parameters $\theta$ with mixing
weights $\pi_k$, means $\mu_k$ and variances $\sigma_k^2$, a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a
component $k$, the responsibility of $k$ for $x$ is the posterior
$p_\theta(k \mid x) = \pi_k \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu_k, \sigma_k^2 I) /
\sum_j \pi_j \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu_j, \sigma_j^2 I)$, where $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, v I)$ is the
isotropic Gaussian density. Computing it at each data point is the E-step.

articles.title: Responsibilities of the full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
For valid parameters
$\theta = (\pi_j, \mu_j, \Sigma_j)_{j\lt K}$, a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a component $k$, write
$p_k(x) = \pi_k \, \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu_k, \Sigma_k)$, where $\mathcal{N}(\cdot \mid \mu, \Sigma)$
is the multivariate Gaussian density. The responsibility of $k$ for $x$ is the posterior
probability of component $k$ given $x$ (the E-step),

$$r_k(x) = \frac{p_k(x)}{\sum_j p_j(x)}.$$

For data $(x_n)_{n\lt N}$ one writes $r_{nk} = r_k(x_n)$.

articles.title: Responsibilities of a Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
Let $\theta$ be valid parameters of a mixture of
$K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions, and write $p_\theta(x, k)$ for the joint probability
of a binary vector $x \in \{0,1\}^d$ and a component $k < K$ under $\theta$. The responsibility of
$k$ for $x$ is the posterior probability $r_k(x) = p_\theta(x, k) / \sum_{k' < K} p_\theta(x, k')$.
Computing it is the E-step of EM.

articles.title: Rich data for a Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
Data $x_0, \dots, x_{N-1} \in \{0,1\}^d$ are rich when
$N > 0$ and, for every coordinate $j < d$, some $x_n$ has $j$-th coordinate $1$ and some $x_m$
has $j$-th coordinate $0$. These are the data on which the M-step yields valid parameters.

articles.title: Responsibility-weighted scatter in an isotropic Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
Given data points
$x_0, \dots, x_{N-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, valid parameters $\theta$ of a $K$-component isotropic
Gaussian mixture and a component $k$, the scatter of $k$ is
$S_k = \sum_n r_{nk} \lVert x_n - \mu_k' \rVert^2$, where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of
component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$, $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$ and
$\mu_k' = N_k^{-1} \sum_n r_{nk} x_n$ is the responsibility-weighted mean.

articles.title: Data that span the space affinely
articles.statement:
A family $(x_n)_{n\lt N}$ of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$
is in general position when it has at least one point ($N > 0$) and is not contained in an
affine hyperplane: for every nonzero $v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ there are indices $n, n'$ with
$\langle v, x_n \rangle \neq \langle v, x_{n'} \rangle$.

On such data every responsibility-weighted sample covariance is positive definite.

articles.title: The weight update maximizes the weights term of the full-covariance mixture
articles.statement:
Let
$(x_n)_{n\lt N}$ be data in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $N > 0$, let $\theta$ be valid parameters, and let
$N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$, where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$. Then for
all real weights $w_k > 0$ with $\sum_k w_k = 1$,

$$\sum_k N_k \log w_k \le \sum_k N_k \log \frac{N_k}{N}.$$

The proof is Gibbs' inequality.

articles.title: Isotropic Gaussian mixtures: the weight update maximizes the weights term
articles.statement:
Let
$x_1, \dots, x_N$ be $N > 0$ points of $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\theta$ be valid parameters of a
$K$-component isotropic Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions, and let $N_k = \sum_n r_{nk}$ be the
mass of component $k$, where $r_{nk}$ is the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under
$\theta$. Then for all real $w_1, \dots, w_K > 0$ with $\sum_k w_k = 1$,

$$\sum_k N_k \log w_k \le \sum_k N_k \log \frac{N_k}{N}.$$

That is, the M-step weights $N_k / N$ maximize the weights term (Gibbs' inequality).

articles.title: The weighted log-likelihood is bounded by its value at the normalized counts
articles.statement:
Let $Z$ be
a finite set, let $c \colon Z \to \mathbb{R}$ be nonnegative counts with positive total
$C = \sum_{z \in Z} c_z > 0$, and let $w \colon Z \to \mathbb{R}$ be positive weights with
$\sum_{z \in Z} w_z = 1$. Then $\sum_{z \in Z} c_z \log w_z \le \sum_{z \in Z} c_z \log(c_z / C)$
(Gibbs' inequality).

When every count is positive the normalized counts $c_z / C$ are themselves admissible weights,
so they maximize.

articles.title: With positive total weight, the weighted mean minimizes the weighted sum of squared distances
articles.statement:
**With positive total weight, the weighted mean minimizes the weighted sum of squared
distances.** Let $F$ be a real inner product space, $s$ a finite index set, $w_i \in \mathbb{R}$
weights with $W = \sum_{i \in s} w_i > 0$, and $x_i \in F$ points for $i \in s$, and let
$m = W^{-1} \sum_{i \in s} w_i x_i$ be the weighted mean. Then for every $c \in F$,

$$\sum_{i \in s} w_i \|x_i - m\|^2 \le \sum_{i \in s} w_i \|x_i - c\|^2.$$

The individual weights need not be nonnegative; only their total is assumed positive.

articles.title: The weighted centroid decomposition
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a real inner product space, $s$ a finite
index set, $w_i \in \mathbb{R}$ weights with $W = \sum_{i \in s} w_i \ne 0$, and $x_i \in F$
points for $i \in s$, and let $m = W^{-1} \sum_{i \in s} w_i x_i$. Then for every $c \in F$,

$$\sum_{i \in s} w_i \|x_i - c\|^2 = \sum_{i \in s} w_i \|x_i - m\|^2 + W \|m - c\|^2.$$

This is the weighted version of the centroid decomposition behind $k$-means. When $W > 0$ it
shows that $m$ minimizes $c \mapsto \sum_{i \in s} w_i \|x_i - c\|^2$.

articles.title: Validity of isotropic Gaussian mixture parameters
articles.statement:
Parameters of a $K$-component
isotropic Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions, with mixing weights $\pi_k$, means $\mu_k$ and
variances $\sigma_k^2 \ge 0$, are valid when every $\pi_k > 0$, $\sum_k \pi_k = 1$, and every
$\sigma_k^2 > 0$.

articles.title: Validity of full-covariance Gaussian mixture parameters
articles.statement:
Parameters
$(\pi_k, \mu_k, \Sigma_k)_{k\lt K}$ of a $K$-component Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions are valid
when every weight $\pi_k$ is positive, the weights sum to one, and every covariance matrix
$\Sigma_k$ is positive definite.

articles.title: The parameter space of isotropic Gaussian mixture EM
articles.statement:
For a $K$-component isotropic
Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions, the parameter space of EM is the set of parameters (mixing
weights $\pi_k$, means $\mu_k \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and variances $\sigma_k^2 \ge 0$) that are
valid: every $\pi_k > 0$, $\sum_k \pi_k = 1$, and every $\sigma_k^2 > 0$.

articles.title: Valid parameters of a full-covariance Gaussian mixture
articles.statement:
The parameter space of EM for the
$K$-component Gaussian mixture in $d$ dimensions with full covariances is the set of parameters
$(\pi_k, \mu_k, \Sigma_k)_{k\lt K}$ that are valid: every weight $\pi_k$ is positive, the weights
sum to one, and every covariance matrix $\Sigma_k$ is positive definite.

articles.title: The parameter space of a Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
The parameter space of EM for a mixture of
$K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions is the set of valid parameters: mixing weights
$\pi_k$ and success probabilities $p_{kj}$ ($k < K$, $j < d$) with every $\pi_k > 0$,
$\sum_{k < K} \pi_k = 1$ and every $p_{kj}$ strictly between $0$ and $1$.

articles.title: Valid parameters of a Bernoulli mixture
articles.statement:
Parameters of a mixture of $K$ products of $d$
Bernoulli distributions, with mixing weights $\pi_k$ and success probabilities $p_{kj}$, are valid
when $\pi_k > 0$ for every $k < K$, $\sum_{k < K} \pi_k = 1$, and $0 < p_{kj} < 1$ for every
$k < K$ and $j < d$.

articles.title: Responsibility-weighted count of zeros
articles.statement:
Let $\theta$ be valid parameters of a mixture of
$K$ products of $d$ Bernoulli distributions, let $x_0, \dots, x_{N-1} \in \{0,1\}^d$ be data, and
let $k < K$ be a component and $j < d$ a coordinate. Write $x_{nj}$ for the $j$-th coordinate of
$x_n$ and $r_k(x_n)$ for the responsibility of component $k$ for $x_n$ under $\theta$. The
weighted count is $\sum_{n < N,\ x_{nj} = 0} r_k(x_n)$, the sum of the responsibilities over the
points whose $j$-th coordinate is $0$.

articles.title: Importance sampling is unbiased
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$, let $\rho$ be a
measure on $\alpha$, let $w : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ be measurable with $w < \infty$
$\rho$-almost everywhere, and let $\nu$ be the measure with density $w$ with respect to $\rho$.
Let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable and integrable with respect to $\nu$. If
$X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega \to \alpha$ are measurable and the pushforward of $\mu$ along each
$X_i$ is $\rho$, then for every $n \ne 0$ the integral with respect to $\mu$ of the
importance-sampling estimate of $f$ with weight $w$ from the first $n$ samples equals
$\int f \, d\nu$.

articles.title: The Monte Carlo estimator is unbiased
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$, let $
u$ be a
measure on $\alpha$, and let $f : \alpha 	o \mathbb{R}$ be measurable and integrable with respect
to $
u$. If $X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega 	o \alpha$ are measurable and the pushforward of $\mu$
along each $X_i$ is $
u$, then for every $n 
e 0$ the integral with respect to $\mu$ of the
Monte Carlo estimate $ rac{1}{n} \sum_{i < n} f(X_i)$ equals $\int f \, d
u$.

articles.title: Change of measure for importance weights
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a measure on $\alpha$, let
$w : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ be measurable with $w < \infty$ $\rho$-almost everywhere, and let
$\nu$ be the measure with density $w$ with respect to $\rho$. Then for every function
$f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, $\int w f \, d\rho = \int f \, d\nu$.

articles.title: Importance-sampling estimate
articles.statement:
Given a weight $w : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$, a function
$f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and samples $X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega \to \alpha$, the
importance-sampling estimate from the first $n$ samples at $\omega \in \Omega$ is
$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i < n} w(X_i(\omega)) \, f(X_i(\omega))$, where an infinite weight counts as
$0$ and the estimate is $0$ when $n = 0$. If the samples are drawn from a proposal measure
$\rho$, it estimates $\int f \, d\nu$ for the target measure $\nu$ with density $w$ with respect to
$\rho$.

articles.title: Monte Carlo estimate
articles.statement:
Given a function $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and samples
$X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega \to \alpha$, the Monte Carlo estimate from the first $n$ samples at
$\omega \in \Omega$ is $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i < n} f(X_i(\omega))$, which is $0$ when $n = 0$.

articles.title: Importance sampling is consistent
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$, let $\rho$ be a
measure on $\alpha$, let $w : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ be measurable with $w < \infty$
$\rho$-almost everywhere, and let $\nu$ be the measure with density $w$ with respect to $\rho$.
Let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable and integrable with respect to $\nu$. If
$X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega \to \alpha$ are measurable, pairwise independent under $\mu$, and the
pushforward of $\mu$ along each $X_i$ is $\rho$, then for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ the
importance-sampling estimate of $f$ with weight $w$ from the first $n$ samples at $\omega$
converges to $\int f \, d\nu$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: The Monte Carlo estimator is consistent
articles.statement:
**The Monte Carlo estimator is consistent** (strong law of large numbers). Let $\mu$ be a
measure on $\Omega$, let $\nu$ be a measure on $\alpha$, and let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be
measurable and integrable with respect to $\nu$. If $X_0, X_1, \ldots : \Omega \to \alpha$ are
measurable, pairwise independent under $\mu$, and the pushforward of $\mu$ along each $X_i$ is
$\nu$, then for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ the Monte Carlo estimate
$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i < n} f(X_i(\omega))$ converges to $\int f \, d\nu$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Acceptance probability
articles.statement:
Given probability mass functions $p$ and $q$ on a type $\alpha$, a
constant $M \in [0, \infty]$ and a point $x \in \alpha$, the acceptance probability of the proposal
$x$ is $p(x) / (M\,q(x))$, computed in $[0, \infty]$, where $a / 0 = \infty$ for $a \ne 0$ and
$0 / 0 = 0$.

articles.title: Biased coin
articles.statement:
For $r \in [0, \infty]$ with $r \le 1$, the biased coin with parameter $r$ is
the probability mass function on $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that gives $\mathrm{true}$
probability $r$ and $\mathrm{false}$ probability $1 - r$.

articles.title: Uniqueness for the first-step equation of rejection sampling
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be
probability mass functions on $\alpha$ and $M \in [0, \infty]$ with $M \ne 0$, $M \ne \infty$ and
$p(y) \le M\,q(y)$ for all $y \in \alpha$. For one round of rejection sampling for target $p$,
proposal $q$ and envelope $M$, write $P(x, \mathrm{accepted})$ for the probability that the round
proposes $x$ and accepts it, and $r$ for the sum over $y \in \alpha$ of the probabilities that it
proposes $y$ and rejects it. If $f \colon \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ takes only finite values and
satisfies $f(x) = P(x, \mathrm{accepted}) + r \, f(x)$ for every $x \in \alpha$, then $f(x) = p(x)$
for every $x \in \alpha$.

The law of the output of the loop that repeats independent rounds until one accepts satisfies this
first-step equation, so this result identifies that law as $p$.

articles.title: Probability that a round proposes and accepts a given point
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be probability
mass functions on $\alpha$ and $M \in [0, \infty]$ with $p(y) \le M\,q(y)$ for all $y \in \alpha$.
For every $x \in \alpha$, one round of rejection sampling for target $p$, proposal $q$ and envelope
$M$ yields the pair $(x, \mathrm{true})$, that is, proposes $x$ and accepts it, with probability
$p(x) / M$.

articles.title: Conditional on acceptance, the proposal has the target law
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be probability
mass functions on $\alpha$ and $M \in [0, \infty]$ with $M \ne 0$, $M \ne \infty$ and
$p(y) \le M\,q(y)$ for all $y \in \alpha$. For one round of rejection sampling for target $p$,
proposal $q$ and envelope $M$, write $P(x, \mathrm{accepted})$ for the probability that the round
proposes $x$ and accepts it, and
$P(\mathrm{accepted}) = \sum_{y \in \alpha} P(y, \mathrm{accepted})$. Then
$P(x, \mathrm{accepted}) / P(\mathrm{accepted}) = p(x)$ for every $x \in \alpha$.

articles.title: One round of rejection sampling
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be probability mass functions on a type
$\alpha$ (the target and the proposal) and let $M \in [0, \infty]$ be an envelope constant with
$p(x) \le M\,q(x)$ for all $x \in \alpha$. One round of rejection sampling for target $p$, proposal
$q$ and envelope $M$ is the probability mass function on pairs
$(x, b) \in \alpha \times \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ obtained by drawing $x$ from $q$ and
then flipping a coin that lands $b = \mathrm{true}$ ("accepted") with probability
$p(x) / (M\,q(x))$.

articles.title: Rejection sampling outputs the target law
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be probability mass functions on
$\alpha$ and $M \in [0, \infty]$ with $M \ne 0$, $M \ne \infty$ and $p(y) \le M\,q(y)$ for all
$y \in \alpha$. For one round of rejection sampling for target $p$, proposal $q$ and envelope $M$,
write $P(x, \mathrm{accepted})$ for the probability that the round proposes $x$ and accepts it, and
$r$ for the sum over $y \in \alpha$ of the probabilities that it proposes $y$ and rejects it. Then
for every $x \in \alpha$,

$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^k \, P(x, \mathrm{accepted}) = p(x).$$

Here $r^k \, P(x, \mathrm{accepted})$ is the probability that repeating independent rounds until
one accepts outputs $x$ after exactly $k$ rejections, so the output of that loop has law $p$.

articles.title: Probability that a round rejects
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be probability mass functions on $\alpha$
and $M \in [0, \infty]$ with $p(x) \le M\,q(x)$ for all $x \in \alpha$. Let $r$ be the sum over
$x \in \alpha$ of the probabilities that one round of rejection sampling for target $p$, proposal
$q$ and envelope $M$ yields $(x, \mathrm{false})$, that is, the probability that the round rejects.
Then $r + M^{-1} = 1$.

articles.title: Probability that a round accepts
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be probability mass functions on $\alpha$
and $M \in [0, \infty]$ with $p(x) \le M\,q(x)$ for all $x \in \alpha$. The sum over $x \in \alpha$
of the probabilities that one round of rejection sampling for target $p$, proposal $q$ and
envelope $M$ yields $(x, \mathrm{true})$ equals $M^{-1}$; that is, a round accepts with
probability $1 / M$.

articles.title: AdaBoost's hypothesis weight
articles.statement:
A weak hypothesis with weighted error
$\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$ gets the weight
$\alpha(\varepsilon) = \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1 - \varepsilon}{\varepsilon}$.

articles.title: Unrolling the weights
articles.statement:
Run AdaBoost with labels $y$ on $m > 0$ training points and a
weak learner, and let $D_T$ be the weights on the points after $T$ rounds, $Z_t$ the normalizer
of round $t$, and $F_T$ the combined score after $T$ rounds. Then for every $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and
every training point $i$,

$$D_T(i) \cdot m \prod_{t < T} Z_t = \exp(-y_i F_T(i)),$$

where the label $y_i$ is read as $\pm 1$.

articles.title: AdaBoost's weights
articles.statement:
Given labels $y$ on $m$ training points and a weak learner
$\mathrm{wl}$, which maps weights on the points to a hypothesis's predictions on them,
AdaBoost's weights $D_t$ on the points are defined by $D_0(i) = 1/m$ for every point $i$, and
$D_{t+1}$ is the reweighting of $D_t$ by the hypothesis $\mathrm{wl}(D_t)$.

articles.title: Weighted error of an AdaBoost round
articles.statement:
The weighted error $\varepsilon_t$ of round $t$ is the
weighted training error of the weak hypothesis $h_t$ of round $t$ under the weights $D_t$ of
round $t$.

articles.title: Weighted training error
articles.statement:
For labels $y$, weights $D$ and predictions $h$ on $m$ training
points, the weighted training error of $h$ under $D$ is $\sum_{i : h(i) \ne y(i)} D(i)$, the total
weight of the points that $h$ misclassifies.

articles.title: Weak hypothesis of an AdaBoost round
articles.statement:
The weak hypothesis $h_t$ of round $t$ is the weak
learner's output $\mathrm{wl}(D_t)$ on the weights $D_t$ of round $t$.

articles.title: The normalizer of a round is $2\sqrt{\varepsilon(1 - \varepsilon)}$
articles.statement:
Let $y$ be labels on
$m$ training points, $D$ real weights on the points with $\sum_i D(i) = 1$, and $h$ predictions
whose weighted training error $\varepsilon$ under $D$ satisfies $0 < \varepsilon < 1$. Then the
normalizer of the round with weights $D$ and hypothesis $h$ equals
$2\sqrt{\varepsilon(1 - \varepsilon)}$.

articles.title: Normalizer of a boosting round
articles.statement:
For labels $y$, weights $D$ and predictions $h$ on $m$
training points, let $\varepsilon$ be the weighted training error of $h$ under $D$ and
$\alpha = \alpha(\varepsilon)$ the hypothesis weight. The normalizer of the round is

$$Z = \sum_i D(i) \exp(-\alpha\, y_i h_i),$$

where the label $y_i$ and the prediction $h_i$ are read as $\pm 1$.

articles.title: AdaBoost reweighting
articles.statement:
For labels $y$, weights $D$ and predictions $h$ on $m$ training
points, let $\varepsilon$ be the weighted training error of $h$ under $D$,
$\alpha = \alpha(\varepsilon)$ the hypothesis weight and $Z$ the normalizer of the round. The
reweighted weight of point $i$ is

$$D'(i) = \frac{D(i) \exp(-\alpha\, y_i h_i)}{Z},$$

where the label $y_i$ and the prediction $h_i$ are read as $\pm 1$.

articles.title: AdaBoost's combined score
articles.statement:
After $T$ rounds, the combined score of training point $i$ is

$$F_T(i) = \sum_{t < T} \alpha(\varepsilon_t)\, h_t(i),$$

where $\varepsilon_t$ is the weighted error and $h_t$ the weak hypothesis of round $t$,
$\alpha(\varepsilon) = \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1 - \varepsilon}{\varepsilon}$ is the hypothesis
weight, and the prediction $h_t(i)$ is read as $\pm 1$. The final classifier is the sign of
$F_T$.

articles.title: AdaBoost drives the training error down exponentially
articles.statement:
Let AdaBoost run on $m > 0$
training points with labels $y$ and a weak learner with edge $\gamma \ge 0$, that is, one that on
every weighting $D$ of the training points with $D_i > 0$ for all $i$ and $\sum_i D_i = 1$ returns
a hypothesis whose weighted error under $D$ lies in $(0, 1/2 - \gamma]$. Then for every number of
rounds $T$, the training error after $T$ rounds is at most $e^{-2\gamma^2 T}$.

articles.title: The Freund–Schapire bound on AdaBoost's training error
articles.statement:
Let AdaBoost run on $m > 0$
training points with labels $y$ and a weak learner with edge $\gamma \ge 0$, that is, one that on
every weighting $D$ of the training points with $D_i > 0$ for all $i$ and $\sum_i D_i = 1$ returns
a hypothesis whose weighted error under $D$ lies in $(0, 1/2 - \gamma]$. Write $\varepsilon_t$ for
the weighted error of the weak hypothesis of round $t$ under AdaBoost's weights of that round.
Then for every number of rounds $T$, the training error after $T$ rounds is at most
$\prod_{t < T} 2\sqrt{\varepsilon_t (1 - \varepsilon_t)}$.

articles.title: The training error is at most the product of the normalizers
articles.statement:
Let AdaBoost run on
$m > 0$ training points with labels $y$ and an arbitrary weak learner, and write $Z_t$ for the
normalizer of round $t$. Then for every number of rounds $T$, the training error after $T$ rounds
is at most $\prod_{t < T} Z_t$.

articles.title: Training error of AdaBoost
articles.statement:
Let AdaBoost run on $m$ training points with labels $y$,
read labels and predictions as $\pm 1$, and let $F_T$ be the combined score after $T$ rounds.
The training error after $T$ rounds is the number of training points $i$ with
$y_i F_T(i) \le 0$, divided by $m$; in particular a zero score counts as an error.

articles.title: One round's factor is at most `exp (-2 γ²)`
articles.statement:
For real numbers $\varepsilon$ and $\gamma$
with $\gamma \ge 0$ and $\varepsilon \le 1/2 - \gamma$, we have
$2\sqrt{\varepsilon (1 - \varepsilon)} \le e^{-2\gamma^2}$, where the square root of a negative
number is taken to be $0$.

articles.title: The weak-learning assumption
articles.statement:
A weak learner, which maps weights on the $m$ training
points with labels $y$ to a hypothesis on those points, has edge $\gamma$ if for every weighting
$D$ of the training points with $D_i > 0$ for all $i$ and $\sum_i D_i = 1$, the hypothesis it
returns on $D$ has weighted error under $D$ in the interval $(0, 1/2 - \gamma]$.

articles.title: Normalizer of an AdaBoost round
articles.statement:
Run AdaBoost on training points with labels $y$, and
read labels and predictions as $\pm 1$. The normalizer of round $t$ is
$Z_t = \sum_i D_t(i) \exp(-\alpha_t y_i h_t(i))$, where $D_t$ are AdaBoost's weights in round
$t$, $h_t$ is the weak hypothesis of round $t$, and $\alpha_t$ is its weight.

articles.title: The Hedge loss splits at any round
articles.statement:
Fix a learning rate $\eta$ and $n$ experts. For a
finite sequence $\sigma$ of loss vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and weights $w \in \mathbb{R}^n$, write
$L(\sigma, w)$ for the algorithm's total loss over $\sigma$ started from $w$, and $W(\sigma, w)$
for the weights after the rounds of $\sigma$ started from $w$. Then for all such sequences
$\sigma, \sigma'$ and all weights $w$, the loss over the concatenation $\sigma\sigma'$ satisfies
$L(\sigma\sigma', w) = L(\sigma, w) + L(\sigma', W(\sigma, w))$.

articles.title: The second-order Hedge bound
articles.statement:
Let $\eta > 0$, and let $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T$ be loss
vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n$ experts with $\ell_t(j) \ge 0$ for all $t$ and $j$. Run Hedge
with learning rate $\eta$ from unit weights, that is $w_1(j) = 1$ and
$w_{t+1}(j) = w_t(j) e^{-\eta \ell_t(j)}$, and let $x_t(j) = w_t(j) / \sum_k w_t(k)$ be the
distribution played in round $t$. Then for every expert $i$,

$$\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_j x_t(j) \ell_t(j) \le \sum_{t=1}^T \ell_t(i) +
\eta \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_j x_t(j) \ell_t(j)^2 + \frac{\log n}{\eta}.$$

This is Theorem 1.3 of Hazan, *Introduction to Online Convex Optimization*. Unlike the
first-order Hedge loss bound, the losses need not be at most $1$.

articles.title: The Hedge loss bound
articles.statement:
Let $\eta$ be a real number, and let $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T$ be loss
vectors in $[0, 1]^n$ for $n$ experts. Run Hedge with learning rate $\eta$ from unit weights, that
is $w_1(j) = 1$ and $w_{t+1}(j) = w_t(j) e^{-\eta \ell_t(j)}$, and let
$x_t(j) = w_t(j) / \sum_k w_t(k)$ be the distribution played in round $t$. Then for every
expert $i$,

$$(1 - e^{-\eta}) \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_j x_t(j) \ell_t(j) \le \eta \sum_{t=1}^T \ell_t(i) + \log n.$$

For $\eta > 0$, writing $L$ for the algorithm's loss and $L_i$ for expert $i$'s loss, this is
the bound $L \le (\log n + \eta L_i) / (1 - e^{-\eta})$ of Freund and Schapire (after
Littlestone and Warmuth).

articles.title: Loss of the Hedge algorithm
articles.statement:
Let $\eta$ be a learning rate, $w \in \mathbb{R}^n$ initial
weights on $n$ experts and $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T \in \mathbb{R}^n$ the losses of $T$ rounds. Set
$w_1 = w$ and $w_{t+1}(j) = w_t(j) e^{-\eta \ell_t(j)}$. The algorithm's total loss is
$\sum_{t=1}^T \bigl(\sum_j w_t(j) \ell_t(j)\bigr) / \sum_j w_t(j)$, the sum over the rounds of
the weighted average of that round's losses; a round whose total weight is $0$ contributes
$0$.

articles.title: The summed second moments split at any round
articles.statement:
Fix a learning rate $\eta$ and $n$ experts.
For a finite sequence $\sigma$ of loss vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and weights $w \in \mathbb{R}^n$,
write $Q(\sigma, w)$ for the sum over the rounds of $\sigma$ of the weighted second moments of the
losses, started from $w$, and $W(\sigma, w)$ for the weights after the rounds of $\sigma$ started
from $w$. Then for all such sequences $\sigma, \sigma'$ and all weights $w$,
$Q(\sigma\sigma', w) = Q(\sigma, w) + Q(\sigma', W(\sigma, w))$.

articles.title: Summed second moments of the Hedge losses
articles.statement:
Let $\eta$ be a learning rate,
$w \in \mathbb{R}^n$ initial weights on $n$ experts and $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T \in \mathbb{R}^n$
the losses of $T$ rounds. Set $w_1 = w$ and $w_{t+1}(j) = w_t(j) e^{-\eta \ell_t(j)}$. The summed
second moment is $\sum_{t=1}^T \bigl(\sum_j w_t(j) \ell_t(j)^2\bigr) / \sum_j w_t(j)$, the sum over
the rounds of the weighted second moment of that round's losses; a round whose total weight is
$0$ contributes $0$.

articles.title: Losses in the unit interval
articles.statement:
A finite sequence of loss vectors
$\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T \in \mathbb{R}^n$ on $n$ experts has losses in $[0, 1]$ when
$0 \le \ell_t(i) \le 1$ for every round $t$ and every expert $i$.

articles.title: The exponential lies below its chord on the unit interval
articles.statement:
For every real $\eta$ and
every $x \in [0, 1]$, $e^{-\eta x} \le 1 - (1 - e^{-\eta}) x$.

articles.title: Total loss of an expert
articles.statement:
For an expert $i$ among $n$ experts and a finite sequence of loss
vectors $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the total loss of expert $i$ is
$\sum_{t=1}^T \ell_t(i)$.

articles.title: Nonnegative losses
articles.statement:
A finite sequence of loss vectors
$\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T \in \mathbb{R}^n$ on $n$ experts has nonnegative losses when
$\ell_t(i) \ge 0$ for every round $t$ and every expert $i$.

articles.title: Loss of a Hedge round
articles.statement:
For weights $w$ and losses $\ell$ on $n$ experts, the algorithm's
loss in the round is $\left(\sum_i w_i \ell_i\right) / W$, where $W = \sum_i w_i$ is the total
weight. This is its expected loss when it follows expert $i$ with probability $w_i / W$.

articles.title: Weighted second moment of a Hedge round
articles.statement:
For weights $w$ and losses $\ell$ on $n$
experts, the round's weighted second moment is $\left(\sum_i w_i \ell_i^2\right) / W$, where
$W = \sum_i w_i$ is the total weight; that is, $\sum_i x_i \ell_i^2$ for the played distribution
$x = w / W$.

articles.title: A round costs weight in proportion to the algorithm's loss, up to a second-order term
articles.statement:
Let $n > 0$, let $w$ be positive weights on $n$ experts, let $\ell$ be nonnegative losses, and let
$\eta \ge 0$. Let $w'$ be the Hedge update of $w$ with learning rate $\eta$, so that
$w'_i = w_i e^{-\eta \ell_i}$, and let $W$ and $W'$ be the total weights of $w$ and $w'$. Then
$W' \le W \exp(-\eta L + \eta^2 Q)$, where $L$ is the round's loss and $Q$ its weighted second
moment under the weights $w$.

articles.title: A round costs weight in proportion to the algorithm's loss
articles.statement:
Let $n > 0$, let $w$ be
positive weights on $n$ experts, let $\ell$ be losses with $0 \le \ell_i \le 1$ for every $i$, and
let $\eta$ be a real number. Let $w'$ be the Hedge update of $w$ with learning rate $\eta$, so that
$w'_i = w_i e^{-\eta \ell_i}$, and let $W$ and $W'$ be the total weights of $w$ and $w'$. Then
$W' \le W \exp(-(1 - e^{-\eta}) L)$, where $L$ is the round's loss under the weights $w$.

articles.title: Weight decay over a Hedge run, second-order form
articles.statement:
Let $n > 0$ and $\eta \ge 0$. For every
sequence of rounds with nonnegative losses and all positive initial weights $w$ on $n$ experts,
the total weight after running Hedge with learning rate $\eta$ from $w$ is at most
$W \exp(-\eta L + \eta^2 Q)$. Here $W$ is the total weight of $w$, $L$ is the algorithm's total
loss over the rounds and $Q$ is the sum of the rounds' weighted second moments, both for the run
from $w$ with learning rate $\eta$.

articles.title: Weight decay over a Hedge run
articles.statement:
Let $n > 0$ and let $\eta$ be a real number. For every
sequence of rounds with losses in $[0, 1]$ and all positive initial weights $w$ on $n$ experts,
the total weight after running Hedge with learning rate $\eta$ from $w$ is at most
$W \exp(-(1 - e^{-\eta}) L)$, where $W$ is the total weight of $w$ and $L$ is the algorithm's
total loss over the rounds for the run from $w$ with learning rate $\eta$.

articles.title: Total weight of the Hedge experts
articles.statement:
The total weight of weights $w$ on $n$ experts is
$\sum_i w_i$.

articles.title: Hedge weight update
articles.statement: After a round with losses `ℓ`, each expert's weight is multiplied by `exp (-η ℓ i)`.

articles.title: A Hedge run splits at any round
articles.statement:
For every learning rate $\eta$, sequences of rounds
$\lambda$ and $\lambda'$, and initial weights $w$, the weights after running Hedge on the rounds of
$\lambda$ followed by those of $\lambda'$, starting from $w$, equal the weights after running it on
$\lambda'$ starting from the weights reached after $\lambda$ from $w$.

articles.title: Closed form of the Hedge weights
articles.statement:
For every learning rate $\eta$, sequence of rounds,
initial weights $w$ and expert $i$, the weight of expert $i$ after running Hedge on the rounds from
$w$ is $w_i e^{-\eta L_i}$, where $L_i$ is expert $i$'s total loss over the rounds.

articles.title: Hedge weights after a sequence of rounds
articles.statement:
Let $\eta \in \mathbb{R}$ be a learning rate,
let $w \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be initial weights on $n$ experts, and let $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_T \in
\mathbb{R}^n$ be the loss vectors of $T$ rounds, given as a list. The weights after these rounds
are obtained from $w$ by applying the Hedge update once per round, in the order of the list:
round $t$ multiplies the weight of each expert $i$ by $e^{-\eta \ell_t(i)}$. For the empty list
of rounds the weights are $w$.

articles.title: A mistake-free pass classifies every example
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring with a linear
order, $\iota$ a finite type, and $v \cdot w = \sum_{i \in \iota} v_i w_i$ the dot product on
$K^\iota$. Let $L$ be a finite list of labelled examples $(x, y)$ with $x \in K^\iota$ and $y$ a
Boolean, and let $w \in K^\iota$. If the perceptron run over $L$ from weights $w$ with $0$ mistakes
so far ends with mistake count $0$, then every example $(x, y)$ in $L$ satisfies
$0 < \operatorname{sign}(y)\,(w \cdot x)$.

articles.title: Every failed training pass adds a mistake
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring with a linear
order and $\iota$ a finite type, and let $L$ be a finite list of labelled examples $(x, y)$ with
$x \in K^\iota$ and $y$ a Boolean. For every natural number $n$ and all weights $w \in K^\iota$, if
training on $L$ from $w$ with at most $n$ passes returns no weights, then the perceptron run from
$w$ with $0$ mistakes so far over the concatenation of $n$ copies of $L$ ends with a mistake count
of at least $n$.

articles.title: Novikoff's mistake bound over an ordered field
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a linearly ordered field,
$\iota$ a finite type, $v \cdot w = \sum_{i \in \iota} v_i w_i$ the dot product on $F^\iota$,
$u \in F^\iota$, and $\gamma, R \in F$ with $\gamma > 0$. Let $L$ be a finite list of labelled
examples $(x, y)$ with $x \in F^\iota$ and $y$ a Boolean, such that every example in $L$ satisfies
$\gamma \le \operatorname{sign}(y)\,(u \cdot x)$ and $x \cdot x \le R^2$. If the perceptron run
over $L$ from the zero weights with $0$ mistakes so far ends with mistake count $k$, then
$k \le (u \cdot u) R^2 / \gamma^2$; for a unit vector $u$ this is the textbook bound
$R^2 / \gamma^2$.

articles.title: Novikoff's perceptron mistake bound
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a linearly ordered commutative ring,
$\iota$ a finite type, $v \cdot w = \sum_{i \in \iota} v_i w_i$ the dot product on $K^\iota$,
$u \in K^\iota$, and $\gamma, R \in K$ with $\gamma > 0$. Let $L$ be a finite list of labelled
examples $(x, y)$ with $x \in K^\iota$ and $y$ a Boolean, such that every example in $L$ satisfies
$\gamma \le \operatorname{sign}(y)\,(u \cdot x)$ and $x \cdot x \le R^2$. If the perceptron run
over $L$ from the zero weights with $0$ mistakes so far ends with mistake count $k$, then
$k \gamma^2 \le (u \cdot u) R^2$.

articles.title: The starting mistake count only shifts the final count
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring
with a linear order and $\iota$ a finite type, and let $L$ be a finite list of labelled examples
$(x, y)$ with $x \in K^\iota$ and $y$ a Boolean. For all weights $w \in K^\iota$ and every natural
number $m$, the perceptron run over $L$ from $w$ with $m$ mistakes so far ends with the same weights
as the run from $w$ with $0$ mistakes so far, and with mistake count $m + c$, where $c$ is the final
mistake count of the run from $w$ with $0$ mistakes so far.

articles.title: Invariant of the perceptron run
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a linearly ordered commutative ring, $\iota$ a
finite type, $v \cdot w = \sum_{i \in \iota} v_i w_i$ the dot product on $K^\iota$, $u \in K^\iota$
and $\gamma, R \in K$. Let $L$ be a finite list of labelled examples $(x, y)$ with $x \in K^\iota$
and $y$ a Boolean, such that every example in $L$ satisfies
$\gamma \le \operatorname{sign}(y)\,(u \cdot x)$ and $x \cdot x \le R^2$. Let $w \in K^\iota$ and
$m \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $m \gamma \le u \cdot w$ and $w \cdot w \le m R^2$, and let the
perceptron run over $L$ from $w$ with $m$ mistakes so far end with weights $w'$ and mistake count
$m'$. Then $m' \gamma \le u \cdot w'$ and $w' \cdot w' \le m' R^2$.

articles.title: Perceptron run
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring with a linear order and $\iota$ a finite type.
The run of the perceptron over a finite list $L$ of labelled examples $(x, y)$, with
$x \in K^\iota$ and $y$ a Boolean, from weights $w \in K^\iota$ with $m \in \mathbb{N}$ mistakes so
far is the pair of final weights and final mistake count obtained by applying the perceptron step
to each example of $L$ in order, starting from the state $(w, m)$.

articles.title: Sign of a Boolean label
articles.statement:
