transition from $p$ to $p'$ with label $\mu$, then there is a state $q'$ with a rooted weak
transition from $q$ to $q'$ with label $\mu$ such that $p'$ and $q'$ are weakly bisimilar.

articles.title: Observation congruence is an equivalence relation
articles.statement:
In every labelled transition system
with a silent label $\tau$, rooted weak bisimilarity (observation congruence) is reflexive,
symmetric and transitive.

articles.title: Strong bisimilarity implies observation congruence
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with
a silent label $\tau$, any two strongly bisimilar states are rooted weakly bisimilar.

articles.title: Transitions are rooted weak transitions
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a silent
label $\tau$, every transition $s \xrightarrow{\mu} t$ is a rooted weak transition from $s$ to $t$
with label $\mu$.

articles.title: Silent steps before a rooted weak transition
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a
silent label $\tau$, if $s$ reaches $m$ by zero or more $\tau$-transitions and there is a rooted
weak transition from $m$ to $t$ with label $\mu$, then there is a rooted weak transition from $s$
to $t$ with label $\mu$.

articles.title: Rooted weak transition
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system whose labels include a silent
label $\tau$, there is a rooted weak transition from $s$ to $t$ with label $\mu$ when there are
states $s_1$ and $s_2$ such that $s$ reaches $s_1$ by zero or more $\tau$-transitions,
$s_1 \xrightarrow{\mu} s_2$ is a transition, and $s_2$ reaches $t$ by zero or more
$\tau$-transitions. In particular, a rooted weak transition with label $\tau$ contains at least
one actual $\tau$-transition.

articles.title: Rooted observation congruence
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a silent label
$\tau$, states $p$ and $q$ are rooted weakly bisimilar (observation congruent) when every
transition $p \xrightarrow{\mu} p'$ is matched by a rooted weak transition from $q$ to some $q'$
with label $\mu$ such that $p'$ and $q'$ are weakly bisimilar, and every transition
$q \xrightarrow{\mu} q'$ is matched by a rooted weak transition from $p$ to some $p'$ with label
$\mu$ such that $p'$ and $q'$ are weakly bisimilar.

articles.title: Observation congruence implies weak bisimilarity
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with
a silent label $\tau$, any two rooted weakly bisimilar states are weakly bisimilar.

articles.title: Rooted weak transitions are weak transitions
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with a
silent label $\tau$, every rooted weak transition from $s$ to $t$ with label $\mu$ is a weak
transition from $s$ to $t$ with label $\mu$, where a weak transition with label $\mu$ is either
the trivial step from a state to itself with label $\tau$, or a transition with label $\mu$
preceded and followed by zero or more $\tau$-transitions.

articles.title: A rooted silent step followed by a weak transition is rooted
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition
system with a silent label $\tau$, if there is a rooted weak transition from $s$ to $m$ with
label $\tau$ and a weak transition from $m$ to $t$ with label $\mu$, then there is a rooted weak
transition from $s$ to $t$ with label $\mu$. Here a weak transition with label $\mu$ is either
the trivial step from a state to itself with label $\tau$, or a transition with label $\mu$
preceded and followed by zero or more $\tau$-transitions.

The initial rooted transition supplies the required actual silent step even when the following
weak transition is reflexive.

articles.title: Appending silent steps to a rooted weak transition
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with
silent action $\tau$, if there is a rooted weak transition from $s$ to $m$ with label $a$, and $t$
is reachable from $m$ by zero or more $\tau$-transitions, then there is a rooted weak transition
from $s$ to $t$ with label $a$.

articles.title: Transitivity of rooted observational congruence
articles.statement:
In a labelled transition system with
silent action $\tau$, if $p$ is rooted observationally congruent to $q$ and $q$ is rooted
observationally congruent to $r$, then $p$ is rooted observationally congruent to $r$.

articles.title: Dual session typing of a binary configuration
articles.statement:
Locally linear threads owning opposite roles on every channel.
Dual compatibility permits cyclic waits; it does not assert progress.

articles.title: Communication step of a binary configuration
articles.statement: Opposite head guards synchronize, in either endpoint orientation.

articles.title: Communication preserves binary session typing
articles.statement:
Communication consumes dual heads and preserves linear residual typing;
payload substitution never changes the session context.

articles.title: Injectivity of the binary configuration embedding
articles.statement: The representation does not identify distinct configurations.

articles.title: Session communication steps are π-calculus reductions
articles.statement: Every session communication is a reduction in the unchanged π semantics.

articles.title: Binary configuration as a parallel composition
articles.statement: Embed a binary configuration without changing either process.

articles.title: Advancing one endpoint of a session context
articles.statement: Advance just the communicating endpoint; other obligations are unchanged.

articles.title: Session-typed threads are well scoped
articles.statement:
Every typed thread satisfies the shared π name/process scoping predicate.
Free session constants remain permitted; this is not ν-closedness.

articles.title: Per-channel session context of a thread
articles.statement: One linear endpoint obligation per physical channel in a thread.

articles.title: Dualizing a context commutes with advancing an endpoint
articles.statement: Advancing dual endpoints preserves pointwise compatibility.

articles.title: Pointwise dual of a session context
articles.statement: The opposite endpoint roles, pointwise.

articles.title: Session type duality is an involution
articles.statement: Duality is an involution, including at completion.

articles.title: Dual of a session type
articles.statement: Exchange the endpoint's send and receive obligations.

articles.title: Session typing derivations have finite support
articles.statement:
A derivation has only finitely many active channel obligations: above
some bound every channel is completed. Contexts are total functions.

articles.title: Linear session typing of sequential threads
articles.statement:
Linear typing of finite sequential threads in the existing π syntax.
`nil` consumes only completed obligations. Input-bound names are unrestricted
payloads, never session subjects; there is no parallel duplication rule.

articles.title: Dual session types have equal length
articles.statement: Opposite endpoint roles have the same number of actions.

articles.title: Length of a session type
articles.statement: Number of communication actions remaining in a finite protocol.

articles.title: Finite binary session types
articles.statement: Finite binary protocols carrying unrestricted, passive names.

articles.title: Payload substitution at any cutoff preserves session typing
articles.statement:
Capture-avoiding payload substitution preserves every linear obligation,
including through nested input binders and at nonzero cutoffs.

articles.title: Receiving a closed name preserves session typing
articles.statement: Receiving a closed name preserves the residual thread's typing.

articles.title: The only active channel is the designated one
articles.statement: Every active endpoint of a single-channel thread is the designated one.

articles.title: Advancing the sole channel keeps the single-channel condition
articles.statement: Communication on the sole session cannot create another dependency.

articles.title: Completed sole protocol means both threads are nil
articles.statement: A completed sole protocol means both threads have reached `nil`.

articles.title: Dual context keeps the single active channel
articles.statement: Opposite roles have the same active-channel support.

articles.title: Typed thread with completed obligations is nil
articles.statement: A typed thread whose endpoint obligations are completed is inert.

articles.title: Finite completion of isolated finite binary sessions
articles.statement:
Every isolated finite dual session admits a finite communication path to
completion. This excludes recursion and is not global π normalization.

articles.title: Progress for dual single-channel session threads
articles.statement:
Dual single-channel threads have either completed or can synchronize.
The single-channel hypothesis excludes cross-session dependency cycles.

articles.title: Receive obligation on the sole channel forces an input guard
articles.statement: A receive obligation forces an input guard on the sole active channel.

articles.title: Session communication paths are π-calculus reduction paths
articles.statement: Paths of session communication are paths of existing π reductions.

articles.title: Send obligation on the sole channel forces an output guard
articles.statement: A send obligation forces a send guard on the sole active channel.

articles.title: Single active channel condition for a session context
articles.statement: All active obligations of this thread belong to one physical channel.

articles.title: Existence of a least-rank active binding
articles.statement:
A nonempty collection of active finite-map bindings has a least rank.
The witness ranges over ALL active roles, not only input guards.

articles.title: Active delegated payloads rank after the guard
articles.statement: Every active delegated payload is included in the pre-transfer guard check.

articles.title: Send heads are active for both payload sorts
articles.statement: Every literal communication head is active, for both payload sorts.

articles.title: Binding a fresh dual pair preserves balance
articles.statement:
A fresh private pair preserves full dual ownership of an outer balanced
interface. Every nonfresh owned role is reflected through canonical lifting.

articles.title: Completed ranked frontiers are congruent to nil
articles.statement:
A frontier with no active ownership cannot contain a live prefix.
Completion is the PROCESS congruence to nil, not a completed empty interface.

articles.title: Structural congruence preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Every canonical Cong constructor preserves the whole priority refinement
at exactly the same context and ambient depth. Unsupported sum/replication
constructors are impossible by the invariant DERIVED from refinement typing.

articles.title: Duality preserves activity of a capability
articles.statement: Activity is preserved by protocol duality, including regular unfolding.

articles.title: Erasing a key whose name is absent preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Actual all-position physical-name absence permits erasure in the
refinement too. Subject and payload lookup obligations are never discarded.

articles.title: Erasing a role preserves the guard condition
articles.statement: Erasing a role can only remove a dependency from a guard check.

articles.title: Minimum active role is the subject of a frontier leaf
Every finite linear π term has a frontier normal form
articles.statement:
GENERAL normalization of every finite-linear existing π term. Prefix
bodies are not evaluated or replaced, and no complementary ready pair is assumed.

articles.title: Ranked-typed processes have a typed frontier normal form
articles.statement:
Ranked normalization is DERIVED from typing, preserving every guard and
all external ownership while exposing all unguarded private restrictions.

articles.title: Frontier normal form of finite networks
articles.statement:
A finite network normal form has all unguarded restrictions outside its
parallel frontier. The binder tower can have any finite depth.

articles.title: Parallel guard frontier
articles.statement:
A parallel frontier consists of nil and actual input/output guards.
No restriction is hidden under parallel; guarded continuations are unrestricted.

articles.title: An active same-rank peer violates the guard condition
articles.statement: Owning an active peer of the guard at the same rank violates the discipline.

articles.title: A guard owning only its own endpoint satisfies the condition
articles.statement:
A guard with only its own endpoint is permitted to keep using that
endpoint sequentially at the same rank. Only DIFFERENT keys must rank later.

articles.title: Guard priority condition on active endpoints
articles.statement:
A guard precedes every other active owned endpoint. Transferred payloads
are included in ownership until transfer; no enabled edge is assumed.

articles.title: Forgetting priorities recovers endpoint typing
articles.statement: Forgetting priorities recovers the exact existing ownership judgement.

articles.title: Ranked head communication yields a dual advance
articles.statement:
For a ranked-typed opposite-head pair at a compatible initial interface,
the head result yields one faithful update and compatible ranked residual,
not a typing witness manufactured by forgetting the refinement.

articles.title: Ranked head communication exposes peers and residual typing
articles.statement:
A ranked-typed opposite-head pair at an initially compatible interface
yields the actual subject/dual-peer heads, payload metadata and exact ranked
continuation context after literal communication.

articles.title: Ranked input subjects are active
articles.statement: Literal input subjects likewise own active receive heads.

articles.title: Ranked input exposes its subject's guard condition
articles.statement: Input inversion exposes the priority constraint before either kind of receive.

articles.title: Inversion of ranked input typing
articles.statement: Ranked input inversion retains both literal payload sorts and all guards.

articles.title: Active roles on other names rank after an input subject
articles.statement: Every other active owned role must rank strictly after an input subject.

articles.title: Adding a completed role preserves the guard condition
articles.statement:
Adding a genuinely completed role introduces no guard dependency.
Completion is checked by the actual unfolded protocol, not a key exemption.

articles.title: Adding a role unused by the partner preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Moving a partner-owned role back requires actual absence to DERIVE
completion from plain typing before refined completed weakening is applied.

articles.title: Lifting preserves frontier normal form
articles.statement: Lifting preserves the restriction tower and increments cutoff under binders.

articles.title: Binder lifting preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Canonical binder lifting preserves every priority and endpoint rank.

articles.title: Lifting preserves guard frontiers
articles.statement: Lifting maps every frontier subject, payload and guarded continuation.

articles.title: A minimum active role owned by a guard is its subject key
articles.statement:
A minimum active role owned by a prefix must be that prefix's exact
subject key, not merely a same-name role. Every other key ranks later.

articles.title: Minimum guard leaf cannot own its dual peer
articles.statement:
A minimum active role's peer cannot be owned by the same guard leaf.
Equal-rank opposite keys violate the actual pre-action GuardMin constraint.

articles.title: Nil typing lifts to ranked typing
articles.statement: Nil has no guard: its refinement is exactly the base completed/scoped context.

articles.title: Restriction inversion for ranked typing
articles.statement: Refinement retains the exact protocol/rank pair installed by restriction.

articles.title: Removing a restriction around nil preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Restricting nil is equivalent to its original completed/scoped interface.

articles.title: Restricting nil preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: A completed fresh pair can be introduced around nil without changing guards.

articles.title: Reverse restriction swap preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Reverse restriction swap uses the canonical process involution.

articles.title: Swapping two restrictions preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Swapping the two restrictions preserves all guard constraints by the
GENERAL capture-safe rename theorem and the exact four-role context equation.

articles.title: Ranked output subjects are active
articles.statement:
Literal output subjects have an active protocol, without any stored
reduction or exposed-ready-pair evidence.

articles.title: Ranked output exposes its subject's guard condition
articles.statement: Output inversion exposes the priority constraint for the actual owned subject.

articles.title: Inversion of ranked output typing
articles.statement: Ranked output inversion retains the pre-transfer active payload check.

articles.title: Reverse parallel reassociation preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Reverse reassociation retains exact contexts and guard checks.

articles.title: Parallel reassociation preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Reassociation derives all pairwise disjointness from actual typing.

articles.title: Parallel commutation preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Commutation retains the actual disjoint split and both ranked subterms.

articles.title: Parallel inversion for ranked typing
articles.statement: Refinement preserves the original disjoint parallel ownership split.

articles.title: Removing a parallel nil preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Nil's actual completed ownership can be reattached without new dependencies.

articles.title: Adding a parallel nil preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Nil introduction allocates an empty ownership context, not an active frame.

articles.title: Parallel composition of frontier normal forms normalizes
articles.statement:
Two normalized components combine by actual canonical scope extrusion.
Every private restriction, on either side, is retained in the resulting tower.

articles.title: Global progress of ranked processes at balanced interfaces
articles.statement:
For a ranked-typed process at ANY balanced interface, global progress
holds, including disconnected networks.
All private channels are tracked through the derived restriction tower.
Completion means process congruence to nil, not completion of the interface.

articles.title: Closed ranked networks are completed or can step
articles.statement:
A closed finite ranked network is completed or takes an ACTUAL canonical
step. Ambient passive-name depth is arbitrary; no readiness witness is supplied.

articles.title: Progress for balanced ranked guard frontiers
articles.statement:
GENERAL balanced ranked frontier progress. A minimum over ALL active
owned roles exposes two distinct opposite subject leaves, from which actual
canonical communication follows. Completion is process-level Cong to nil.

articles.title: Endpoint delegation at the head preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
With the stated disjoint ranked split, owned non-carrier scoped payload
and compatible combined interface, delegation derives substitution freshness
from that split and retains the combined payload value.

articles.title: Passive head communication preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
With the stated disjoint ranked split, scoped passive payload and
compatible combined interface, head communication substitutes through the
ranked input body and retains both residual guard derivations.

articles.title: Priority-ranked endpoint typing judgement
articles.statement:
Linear ownership typing with a strict priority check at every guard.
There is no reduction, enabled-edge, progress or preservation field.

articles.title: Reachable states of closed ranked networks stay typed
articles.statement:
Every state reached by finitely many actual canonical steps retains exact
empty-interface ranked typing. This is preservation, not finite termination.

articles.title: Progress at reachable states of closed ranked networks
articles.statement:
Global progress holds at every finite reachable state of a closed ranked
network. No fairness, eventual liveness or recursive termination is asserted.

articles.title: Injective rekeying preserves the guard condition
articles.statement:
Collision-free rekeying preserves guard inequalities and the exact
same-endpoint exemption; it cannot silently identify the peer role.

articles.title: Collision-free renaming preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Physical-name rekeying preserves the entire syntax-directed refinement,
including all guard priorities, passive/endpoint payloads and nested binders.
Injectivity is needed only on owned keys, as in the base ownership judgement.

articles.title: Restoring the bound pair preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Restoring the bound pair adds only absent completed partner roles; all
original active ownership and inequalities of the restricted component remain.

articles.title: Same-name ranked guards are opposite and communicate
articles.statement:
Given disjoint ranked-typed leaves with literal same-name input/output
guard shapes and a compatible combined interface, their directions are opposite.
The Step is canonical commSelect, possibly after parallel commutation.

articles.title: Forward scope extrusion preserves ranked typing
articles.statement: Extrusion lifts the partner's real ownership while retaining every guard.

articles.title: Ranked typing is invariant under scope extrusion
articles.statement: Exact bidirectional canonical scope transport for the same refinement.

articles.title: Reverse scope extrusion preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Reverse extrusion derives the entire outer ownership split from typing,
removes only genuinely absent partner roles and retains all guard inequalities.

articles.title: Ranked subject reduction at balanced interfaces
articles.statement:
For a ranked-typed source, initial balance supplies compatibility and is
preserved by the actual canonical step and its exact update.

articles.title: Ranked subject reduction at the empty interface
articles.statement:
Empty-interface ranked typing is preserved by any canonical step at any
ambient depth and through pre/post congruence. The empty context supplies
balance and therefore the required compatibility.

articles.title: Subject reduction for ranked typing at compatible interfaces
articles.statement:
From a ranked-typed source with an initially compatible interface, every
actual canonical step preserves the refinement and compatibility, with zero
or one actual external matched subject advancement.
Private head/continuation changes are derived from faithful bound projection.

articles.title: Disjoint split supplies freshness for endpoint substitution
articles.statement: The transmitted role's non-aliasing is derived, not a readiness premise.

articles.title: Endpoint substitution preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Endpoint substitution transports every ranked subject and payload guard
with freshness derived from the actual linear ownership split.

articles.title: Passive substitution preserves ranked typing
articles.statement:
Canonical passive substitution transports all priority guards on lifted
outer ownership. The bound name owns no endpoint capability in this case.

articles.title: Ranked typing descends from a lifted process
articles.statement: Reflection of an actual lifted term recovers every priority and context entry.

articles.title: Weakening ranked typing by a disjoint completed context
articles.statement: Reattaching a disjoint completed finite context preserves all guards.

articles.title: Weakening ranked typing by a completed capability
articles.statement:
Adding a fresh completed capability preserves every guard inequality
through all seven rules. No active capability can be added by this theorem.

articles.title: A fresh restriction pair is balanced
articles.statement: A real fresh restriction creates a balanced pair on a single physical name.

articles.title: The empty interface is balanced
articles.statement:
An empty external interface is balanced. Internal ν channels still
require their own balanced ownership and are not thereby completed.

articles.title: Balanced endpoint ownership
articles.statement:
Every owned role has its opposite role at the same physical name, with
the same rank and the dual protocol. This condition may permit deadlocks.

articles.title: Balanced interfaces are compatible
articles.statement: A balanced complete interface supplies compatibility for every present pair.

articles.title: Compatibility of a partial endpoint interface
articles.statement:
A partial interface is compatible if opposite roles, WHEN both are
present, have dual protocols. A missing peer is not an enabled-edge witness.

articles.title: Disjoint owned keys on one name have opposite roles
articles.statement:
A dual-compatible pair of physically equal but disjoint owned keys
must be opposite roles. The runtime channel name alone does not supply this.

articles.title: Rekeying preserves balance
articles.statement:
Capture-safe rekeying transports balance when endpoint roles are retained.
The injectivity condition is on owned keys, not on arbitrary passive data.

articles.title: Compatibility passes to the left part of a union
articles.statement:
Any left subcontext of a compatible interface retains compatibility of
its present pairs; no global-progress assumption is involved.

articles.title: Compatibility passes to the right part of a disjoint split
articles.statement:
A right child of a disjoint linear split inherits compatibility of
its present pairs from the combined interface.

articles.title: Binary session typing embeds into polarized endpoint typing
articles.statement:
Dual original threads embed as disjoint opposite roles on the same
physical constants, with exactly their original finite protocol obligations.

articles.title: Restriction binding over the empty map
articles.statement: In an empty outer context, restriction exposes exactly its two peers.

articles.title: Binding a fresh dual pair under restriction
articles.statement:
A restriction binds one physical name and creates its two distinct
linear roles. Lifted outer keys cannot be overwritten by these insertions.

articles.title: Entries of a restriction-bound ownership map
articles.statement:
The exact restriction context has two fresh entries plus all shifted
outer ownership. No old entry is overwritten by a new endpoint role.

articles.title: Restriction binding preserves absence of an outer key
articles.statement: An absent outer key remains absent after adding the fresh bound dual pair.

articles.title: Lifting preserves absence of a key
articles.statement: Lifting preserves absence of an outer role from its finite context.

articles.title: Both roles of the new name are fresh for a lifted map
articles.statement: Both roles of the newly inserted name are fresh for the lifted context.

articles.title: Lifting the empty ownership map
articles.statement: Inserting a binder does not manufacture an outer capability.

articles.title: Lifting a singleton ownership map
articles.statement: Lifting a single capability shifts its name, not its protocol or role.

articles.title: Lifting an ownership map past a binder
articles.statement: Insert an ambient name binder at any cutoff in an ownership context.

articles.title: Negative role lookup after restriction binding
articles.statement: The same restriction installs the negative peer at the SAME name.

articles.title: Positive role lookup after restriction binding
articles.statement:
Restriction installs the positive capability without losing it to the
opposite role's insertion.

articles.title: Lookups in a lifted ownership map
articles.statement: Lifting keeps the entire capability at the corresponding lifted key.

articles.title: Injectivity of rekeying survives erasing a key
articles.statement: Erasing an owned key cannot create a rekeying collision.

articles.title: Injectivity of rekeying survives updating an owned key
articles.statement: Updating an already-owned key introduces no new aliasing obligation.

articles.title: Injectivity of rekeying under a restriction binding
articles.statement: Both newly restricted roles lie in the collision-free binder domain.

articles.title: Rekeying under a binder is injective on fresh and lifted keys
articles.statement:
Rekeying under a binder is injective on both fresh roles and all lifted
outer ownership, not just on endpoint keys with different physical names.

articles.title: Injectivity of rekeying passes under a binder
articles.statement: Collision freedom of owned keys is stable when entering a binder.

articles.title: Injectivity of rekeying after receiving a fresh role
articles.statement:
A linear input's fresh variable role preserves collision freedom of
all lifted outer keys, including outer keys of the opposite role.

articles.title: Received role's opposite is absent at the bound name
articles.statement: A received role cannot duplicate an existing key of the opposite role.

articles.title: Linear input installs the received role on the bound name
articles.statement: Linear input installs precisely the transmitted role on its bound name.

articles.title: Rekeying commutes with binding a private pair
articles.statement:
Restriction rekeying fixes its newly bound pair and transports exactly
the outer context; it cannot alias either fresh role with an outer key.

articles.title: Rekeying under a binder is the lift of the outer rekeying
articles.statement: Rekeying under a binder is exactly the lift of the outer rekeying.

articles.title: Binder extension fixes the fresh binder's endpoint keys
articles.statement: The fresh binder's endpoint roles are fixed under name transformation.

articles.title: Binder extension commutes with lifting on endpoint keys
articles.statement: Entering a binder commutes with endpoint rekeying and retains its role.

articles.title: Endpoint capability with a dependency rank
articles.statement: One linear protocol obligation with its dependency rank.

articles.title: The empty ownership map is completed
articles.statement: The empty ownership map is completed.

articles.title: Completed ownership map
articles.statement:
A context has no remaining communication obligation. End capabilities
may still be recorded, but an active protocol is never silently discarded.

articles.title: Finite endpoint ownership map
articles.statement: Finite ownership map, indexed by polarized keys rather than names.

articles.title: Injective rekeying preserves disjoint ownership
articles.statement:
Disjoint ownership remains disjoint when the combined owned domain
is rekeyed injectively. Opposite roles are not collapsed to physical names.

articles.title: Capability duality is an involution
articles.statement: Capability duality does not change rank or lose protocol information.

articles.title: Dual of an endpoint capability
articles.statement: The peer's obligation has the same rank and dual subject protocol.

articles.title: Erasing a key preserves completion
articles.statement:
Erasing a key preserves absence of any noncompleted obligation;
the empty map is not itself a completion claim about hidden ν processes.

articles.title: Inserting a completed capability preserves completion
articles.statement: Recording a completed endpoint preserves completion of a finite map.

articles.title: Lookups in a rekeyed ownership map
articles.statement: Rekeying preserves each capability verbatim at its image key.

articles.title: Keys of a rekeyed ownership map
articles.statement: Rekeying has precisely the image of the original owned keys.

articles.title: Rekeying preserves completion
articles.statement: Completed protocols remain completed under collision-free name transport.

articles.title: Rekeying that fixes every owned key fixes the map
articles.statement: Rekeying that fixes all owned keys retains the exact map.

articles.title: Identity rekeying fixes an ownership map
articles.statement: Identity rekeying retains the exact finite map, including end slots.

articles.title: Composition of collision-free rekeyings
articles.statement: Consecutive collision-free rekeyings compose on the same finite map.

articles.title: Collision-free rekeying of an ownership map
articles.statement:
Rekey a finite map when no two owned keys are merged. Global
injectivity is unnecessary, which matters for endpoint substitution.

articles.title: Uniqueness of capability lookups
articles.statement: Two lookups of the same linear key cannot give different capabilities.

articles.title: Structural congruence preserves the finite linear fragment
articles.statement:
All existing structural congruences preserve the finite linear
fragment. In particular, folding replication cannot introduce it.

articles.title: Lifting preserves and reflects the finite linear fragment
articles.statement: Lifting cannot add or remove unsupported process constructors.

articles.title: Selection is trivial on the choice-free fragment
articles.statement: Selection cannot discard a branch of a term in the choice-free fragment.

articles.title: Reduction preserves the finite linear fragment
articles.statement:
All existing π reduction constructors preserve the finite fragment,
including arbitrary pre/post structural congruence and selection.

articles.title: Substitution preserves and reflects the finite linear fragment
articles.statement: Substitution changes names, not the finite fragment's process shape.

articles.title: Restriction swap preserves and reflects the finite linear fragment
articles.statement: Swapping restrictions cannot add or remove choice or replication.

articles.title: Finite linear π fragment without choice or replication
articles.statement: Existing π terms without choice or replication, including their bodies.

articles.title: Restriction binding commutes with erasing an owned outer key
articles.statement: Erasing an owned outer role commutes with restriction's fresh dual pair.

articles.title: Restriction binding commutes with inserting an outer key
articles.statement:
Inserting an outer endpoint before restriction is the same as
inserting its lifted key after the fresh dual pair has been bound.

articles.title: Restriction binding of a disjoint union
articles.statement:
Scope extrusion keeps the dual pair on the restricted component and
lifts exactly the unrelated outer partner ownership.

articles.title: Binding a fresh pair keeps disjointness from a lifted context
articles.statement: A fresh bound pair belongs only to the left component of a lifted split.

articles.title: Erase-and-insert transfer preserves disjointness
articles.statement:
Removing a key from the sender and inserting it at the receiver
preserves disjoint endpoint ownership.

articles.title: Inserting a key absent from the other side preserves disjointness
articles.statement:
An insertion disjoint from the other side preserves a linear split,
including the unused completed slots transported by structural congruence.

articles.title: Updating an owned key preserves a disjoint split
articles.statement: Advancing an already-owned endpoint preserves a disjoint split.

articles.title: Capability transfer with carrier updates preserves disjointness
articles.statement:
Capability transfer is a disjoint ownership move, including when the
sender and receiver also advance their distinct carrier roles.

articles.title: Erasing the bound pair leaves the lifted context
articles.statement:
Removing the two freshly bound roles exposes exactly the lifted
external context, including every unrelated completed resource.

articles.title: Erasing a different key commutes with insertion
articles.statement:
Erasing a different endpoint commutes with insertion, which is needed
when an unused completed slot passes through a delegation prefix.

articles.title: Erasure after inserting the same key
articles.statement: Erasing an inserted key removes its entry, independently of its value.

articles.title: Erasing an absent key changes nothing
articles.statement: Erasing an absent key changes no ownership entry.

articles.title: Erasure distributes over union
articles.statement: Erasure distributes through the exact finite ownership union.

articles.title: Updating an owned key keeps absent keys absent
articles.statement: Advancing another already-owned carrier does not create a payload alias.

articles.title: Owned keys are absent from the other side of a disjoint split
articles.statement: A sent endpoint is absent from the other side of a linear split.

articles.title: Insertion after erasing the same key
articles.statement:
Reinstalling a key overrides any previous entry, so prior erasure of
that same key is immaterial.

articles.title: Reinserting an owned capability changes nothing
articles.statement: Reinstalling exactly an already-owned capability changes no entry.

articles.title: Inserting a left-absent key into a union updates the right part
articles.statement:
Inserting a key absent from the left component updates only the right
component of a left-biased finite-map union.

articles.title: Context lifting commutes with erasing an owned key
articles.statement: Erasing an owned outer key commutes with canonical context lifting.

articles.title: Context lifting commutes with insertion
articles.statement: Context lifting commutes with endpoint advancement at any cutoff.

articles.title: Context lifting preserves a disjoint union
articles.statement: Canonical lifting preserves a disjoint ownership union exactly.

articles.title: Collision-free rekeying commutes with erasing an owned key
articles.statement: Erasing an owned key commutes with collision-free rekeying.

articles.title: Collision-free rekeying commutes with insertion
articles.statement:
Rekeying commutes with capability insertion when the combined domain
has no key collision. The condition is on ownership, not execution.

articles.title: Collision-free rekeying commutes with a disjoint union
articles.statement: Collision-free rekeying commutes with a linear parallel split.

articles.title: Reinstalling the bound pair after erasing its slots
articles.statement:
Reinstalling the bound pair after removing its old slots restores the
same exact map as installing that pair directly.

articles.title: Combined context after delegation and two carrier updates
articles.statement:
Delegation plus two carrier advances preserves every other key in the
combined context; the sent capability is moved, not duplicated or dropped.

articles.title: Moving a capability across a union preserves the union
articles.statement:
Moving a capability out of one map into the other preserves the exact
combined interface, including completed endpoint slots.

articles.title: Updating owned keys on both sides of a disjoint union
articles.statement:
Advancing both peers across a disjoint split advances exactly those
two keys in the combined interface, with no other capability change.

articles.title: Completed finite contexts give completed ownership maps
articles.statement: Original completed contexts have no active finite-map protocol.

articles.title: Ownership maps for opposite roles are disjoint
articles.statement: Opposite finite roles split without duplicating any endpoint key.

articles.title: Lookup in the finite-context ownership map
articles.statement: Exact lookup specification for the finite-resource bridge.

articles.title: Keys of the finite-context ownership map
articles.statement: Finite bridge ownership has exactly the bounded constant keys.

articles.title: Finite ownership map commutes with channel advancement
articles.statement: Advancing an original channel advances precisely its finite-map role.

articles.title: Polarized ownership map of a finite channel context
articles.statement:
Turn finitely many original channel slots into polarized finite-map
ownership. The supplied rank assignment adds no execution hypothesis.

articles.title: Finite guarded regular protocol graph
articles.statement:
Finite presentation of guarded equi-recursive protocols. An empty graph
has no cursor and therefore cannot denote a protocol.

articles.title: Node of a guarded protocol graph
articles.statement:
A graph node: completion or a communication with a bounded continuation.
Endpoint payloads include their role, rank, cursor and protocol orientation.

articles.title: Endpoint-typed processes are scoped at the ambient depth
articles.statement: Every endpoint-typed process satisfies the canonical π scope predicate.

articles.title: Endpoint-typed processes lie in the finite linear fragment
articles.statement: Typed terms stay in the proved Cong/Step-closed finite fragment.

articles.title: Linear endpoint typing of π-calculus processes
articles.statement:
Syntax-directed linear typing. Capabilities never contain preservation
or progress assumptions. Protocol heads may be guarded regular protocols.

articles.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for input
articles.statement:
Input inversion exposes its owned role, literal payload sort, and
continuation context. Passive and delegated names are not conflated.

articles.title: Adding a completed capability at nil preserves typing
articles.statement:
Completed endpoint slots may be added at nil without creating a
communication obligation; active protocols cannot use this rule.

articles.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for nil
articles.statement: Nil inversion exposes completion and scope of every recorded endpoint.

articles.title: Nil is typed by a single capability with completed head
articles.statement:
Any protocol whose guarded head is completed is admissible at a
single nil-owned slot, including completed regular graph cursors.

articles.title: Nil is typed by a single done capability
articles.statement:
A recorded completed capability is admissible at nil; an active one
would fail the completed-context premise.

articles.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for output
articles.statement:
Output inversion exposes the actual owned subject, distinct payload sort,
and literal continuation resources; delegation consumes the payload role.

articles.title: Output subjects of endpoint-typed processes are owned
articles.statement:
Every output subject is backed by an owned role, never merely by a
passive name in the ambient data scope.

articles.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for parallel composition
articles.statement:
Parallel typing exposes an actual disjoint ownership split, not a
stored preservation or progress witness.

articles.title: Finite protocol embedding commutes with duality
articles.statement: The finite embedding preserves both protocol orientations.

articles.title: Injectivity of the finite protocol embedding
articles.statement: Different finite protocols remain different in the richer representation.

articles.title: Embedding of finite passive-name protocols
articles.statement: Embed the original finite passive-name protocol without changing actions.

articles.title: Recovery is a left inverse of the finite embedding
articles.statement: The finite embedding has a literal left inverse.

articles.title: Partial recovery of a finite passive-name protocol
articles.statement:
Recover a finite passive protocol; richer payloads and recursion are
not erased into a falsely finite protocol.

articles.title: Protocol duality is an involution
articles.statement: Duality is involutive for finite and guarded recursive protocols.

articles.title: Dual of an endpoint protocol
articles.statement: Reverse subject actions and continuations; preserve payload ownership.

articles.title: Endpoint protocol with guarded regular recursion
articles.statement:
A protocol with explicit payload sort and guarded graph recursion.
Payload endpoint roles are transmitted unchanged, not dualized.

articles.title: Unfolding commutes with protocol duality
articles.statement: Guarded unfolding commutes with duality, including recursive payloads.

articles.title: Unfolding never yields a regular-cursor protocol
articles.statement:
Unfolding always exposes an action or completion, never another silent
regular-cursor wrapper. Cycles therefore cannot consist only of unfolding.

articles.title: Protocol unfolding is idempotent
articles.statement: One root unfolding is enough to expose a guard or completion.

articles.title: One-step unfolding of a protocol
articles.statement:
Expose one communication guard. Graph successors retain their subject
orientation; an endpoint payload retains its independently specified one.

articles.title: Binding equivalent fresh pairs preserves ownership-map equivalence
articles.statement: A chosen exact dual private pair can be preserved or equivalently changed.

articles.title: Ownership-map equivalence preserves semantic compatibility
articles.statement: Semantic compatibility is invariant, including explicit enclosing ranks.

articles.title: Ownership-map equivalence preserves completion
articles.statement: Completion invariance uses actual unfolded done, not just empty ownership.

articles.title: Pointwise equivalence of ownership maps
articles.statement:
Same lookup domain, identical enclosing capability ranks, and equivalent
protocol trees. No matching split or retyping result is stored.

articles.title: Erasure preserves ownership-map equivalence
articles.statement: Both sides erase precisely the same key.

articles.title: Equivalent insertions preserve ownership-map equivalence
articles.statement: Corresponding insertions preserve literal rank and semantic type equivalence.

articles.title: Lifting preserves ownership-map equivalence
articles.statement: Canonical binder lift preserves corresponding values and exact domains.

articles.title: Lookups in a key projection
articles.statement: Projection retains precisely the actual target binding at a source key.

articles.title: Lookups transfer along ownership-map equivalence
articles.statement: Matching source lookup yields an actual target binding and rank/tree relation.

articles.title: Equivalent ownership maps have the same keys
articles.statement: Exact key-domain invariance.

articles.title: Keys of a projection are the intersection of domains
articles.statement: The projected domain is the exact intersection of actual owned domains.

articles.title: Ownership-map equivalence from two-way lookup correspondence
articles.statement: Bidirectional actual lookup correspondence suffices for Option.Rel.

articles.title: Key projection agrees with the target inside the source domain
articles.statement: Inside a source domain the actual target value is retained verbatim.

articles.title: Key projection is absent outside the source domain
articles.statement: Outside a source domain the projection is literally absent.

articles.title: Projection of an ownership map onto another map's keys
articles.statement:
Restrict actual target bindings to the exact key domain of a source map.
The implementation is canonical multiset filtering, not a new finite map.

articles.title: Equivalence of a union restricts to its left part
articles.statement:
An equivalent whole map induces an equivalent child with the exact source
key domain; no matching target split is supplied by a caller.

The inserted name is absent from every position of the actual lifted
π term, including payloads and all nested input/restriction binders.

articles.title: Absence of a physical name from a process
articles.statement:
The given physical name occurs in no subject, payload or continuation
position. Existing binders shift the tracked outer name with canonical lift.

articles.title: An output payload name is not absent
articles.statement: A transmitted endpoint payload is an occurrence, even when completed.

articles.title: Every π step source has an unguarded input
articles.statement:
Every existing π step requires an exposed input in its source,
including pre-congruence, selection, context closure and replication folding.

articles.title: Substitution cancels name lifting
articles.statement:
Substitution removes an inserted binder without changing its shifted
outer names. The inserted binder's replacement is arbitrary.

articles.title: Substitution cancels process lifting
articles.statement:
Removing an inserted binder cancels lifting throughout the unchanged
π syntax, including nested inputs, restrictions, choice and replication.

articles.title: Injectivity of name swapping
articles.statement: Swapping existing binders cannot identify physical names.

articles.title: Name swap is an involution
articles.statement: Swapping the same two existing binders twice restores a name.

articles.title: Process swap is an involution
articles.statement: Existing process swapping is likewise involutive under every binder.

articles.title: Weakening by an unused completed endpoint
articles.statement:
An unused completed endpoint may be added through every current typing
constructor. Scope and freshness are explicit; active weakening is not admitted.

articles.title: Structural congruence preserves process scoping
articles.statement:
Every existing structural congruence transports canonical π scoping,
including scope extrusion, restriction swapping and replication folding.

articles.title: Lifting preserves and reflects process scoping
articles.statement: Lifting reflects canonical process scoping at an ambient cutoff.

articles.title: Choice selection preserves process scoping
articles.statement:
Selection preserves canonical scope even when actual guarded choices
are present in the existing π syntax.

articles.title: Swapping binders in scope preserves name scoping
articles.statement:
Swapping two binders inside the ambient scope preserves the canonical
name predicate in both directions.

articles.title: Swapping binders in scope preserves process scoping
articles.statement: Scope preservation by swapping extends through every existing binder.

articles.title: Binder lifting preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement:
Any ambient binder lift transports full endpoint typing without
changing protocols, roles or resource multiplicity.

articles.title: Capture-safe renaming preserves process scope
articles.statement: Capture-safe syntax transport preserves the canonical process scope.

articles.title: Process renaming by a lift is process lifting
articles.statement: The generic syntax transformation specializes to the existing π lift.

articles.title: Process renaming by a substitution is process substitution
articles.statement:
Subject and payload substitution are exactly the canonical π operation,
including through all input and restriction binders.

articles.title: Process renaming by a swap is the restriction swap
articles.statement: The generic capture-safe map specializes to the existing π restriction swap.

articles.title: Capture-safe renaming of processes
articles.statement:
Capture-safe name transformation of existing processes. Binder bodies
use `under`; this introduces no new syntax or transition relation.

articles.title: Removing a parallel nil preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement:
Removing a parallel nil reattaches exactly its completed ownership;
no active capability is silently dropped.

articles.title: Collision-free renaming preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement:
Capture-safe rekeying transports all finite-process endpoint typing,
including linear payloads and actual input/ν binders. Collision freedom is
required only on owned keys and can be derived from a delegation split.

articles.title: Extending a lift under a binder raises its cutoff
articles.statement: Under a binder, canonical lifting increases its cutoff by one.

articles.title: Extended name map commutes with lifting outer names
articles.statement: The new binder is fixed and outer names are transformed capture-safely.

articles.title: Extending a scoped name map under a binder keeps it scoped
articles.statement:
Extending a scoped transformation under a binder preserves the
canonical scope relation at the incremented source and target depths.

articles.title: Extending a substitution under a binder raises its cutoff
articles.statement:
Under an existing binder, substitution lifts its replacement and
increments its cutoff, exactly as PiCalculus.substProc does.

articles.title: Extending a swap under a binder shifts both indices
articles.statement: Extending a restriction swap under a binder shifts both swapped indices.

articles.title: Extension of a name map under a binder
articles.statement: Extend a name transformation under one existing input/ν binder.

articles.title: Weakening by a disjoint completed context
articles.statement:
A disjoint completed context can be reattached to any typed process,
with the exact finite-map union required by parallel-nil congruence.

articles.title: Owned capability with an absent name is completed
articles.statement:
An owned capability with no physical-name occurrence must already be
completed. This is derived from typing, including endpoint payload positions.

articles.title: Reduction steps preserve process scoping
articles.statement:
Every existing π step preserves canonical scope, not just direct
head communication. Substitution is the existing capture-avoiding one.

articles.title: Communicating subjects in a compatible split have dual capabilities
articles.statement:
Disjoint complementary subjects in a compatible interface have exactly
dual protocol capabilities, including their ranks and endpoint payload sorts.

articles.title: Communicating subjects in a compatible split have equal ranks
articles.statement:
For disjoint owned same-name roles in a compatible combined interface,
their capability ranks agree, as required by exact capability duality.

articles.title: Dual of an endpoint send head is an endpoint receive head
articles.statement:
Duality preserves a delegated payload's role/rank/protocol while
reversing only the subject continuation.

articles.title: Endpoint-delegating communication preserves typing
articles.statement:
At a compatible combined interface with the stated disjoint typed split,
owned payload distinct from the carrier and scoped payload name, endpoint
communication transfers the payload role once and advances only the carrier.

articles.title: Endpoint typing drops a role whose name does not occur
articles.statement:
A role can be erased when its physical name is absent from every
subject, payload and binder-adjusted continuation position of the typed term.

articles.title: Head communication preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement:
For a typed opposite-head pair at an initially compatible interface,
direct communication in the existing π syntax yields an exact typed residual
ownership context, including endpoint delegation.

articles.title: Passive substitution is injective on lifted outer keys
articles.statement: Passive substitution is collision-free on all lifted outer endpoint keys.

articles.title: Received-endpoint substitution is injective when the role is fresh
articles.statement:
Linear input substitution is collision-free when the transmitted role
was absent from the receiver. Its opposite physical-name role is allowed.

articles.title: Matched output head of a capability
articles.statement: The actual payload kind and continuation of a matched output head.

articles.title: Dual of a passive send head is a passive receive head
articles.statement:
Actual endpoint protocols and rank equality force matching passive
receive guards at a complementary owned role.

articles.title: Passive-payload communication preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement:
At a compatible combined interface with the stated disjoint typed split
and scoped passive payload, head communication advances the two complementary
roles and no other capability in the exact residual context.

articles.title: Passive substitution leaves the linear context unchanged
articles.statement:
Passive input substitution changes no linear context: every owned
key is a lifted outer key, so the input binder owns no endpoint role.

articles.title: Received-endpoint substitution moves the bound role to the sent key
articles.statement:
Subject substitution consumes the bound role and inserts exactly the
sent key, preserving every other capability and permitting its peer role.

articles.title: Capability whose head is a send with a given continuation
articles.statement:
The old subject's actual head determines its literal continuation,
independently of whether the transmitted endpoint is external or ν-bound.

articles.title: Linear subject substitution with freshness from disjoint ownership
articles.statement:
Linear subject substitution with non-aliasing DERIVED from disjoint
sender/receiver ownership and the receiver's already-owned carrier.

articles.title: Endpoint typing under substitution of a transmitted endpoint
articles.statement:
Receiving a linear endpoint substitutes its physical name in ALL
subject and payload positions, removes the bound role and inserts the sent
role exactly once. Capture under input and ν is the canonical π substitution.

articles.title: Substitution cancels lifting on endpoint keys
articles.statement: Substitution cancels binder lift on an entire polarized endpoint key.

articles.title: Endpoint typing under passive name substitution
articles.statement:
Passive payload substitution preserves every linear obligation and
cannot introduce an endpoint subject capability.

articles.title: Dual advancement preserves balance
articles.statement:
Faithful subject advancement retains balance if the initial external
interface is balanced.

articles.title: Matching send and receive heads of two capabilities
articles.statement: Both literal communication heads, with separate payload equivalence.

articles.title: Dual advancement preserves compatibility
articles.statement:
A faithful matched update retains compatibility if the initial
interface is compatible.

articles.title: Dual advancement preserves disjointness from a frame
articles.statement: A matched update leaves a disjoint ownership frame disjoint.

articles.title: Advancement of a matched dual subject pair
articles.statement:
Only two actually matched dual subject capabilities advance. Payload
ownership transfer is invisible in the combined map; all other entries remain.
The payload can be private to a ν binder, so external advancement records its
protocol head rather than demanding external ownership of that payload.

articles.title: Dual-continuation update preserves balance
articles.statement:
Advancing a matched dual pair preserves full balance when the original
interface is balanced, including every untouched opposite-role obligation.

articles.title: Dual-continuation update preserves compatibility
articles.statement:
From a compatible initial interface, updating both subjects to dual
continuations preserves compatibility independently of process typing.

articles.title: Dual-continuation update leaves other lookups unchanged
articles.statement: Outside the two matched subjects, the entire capability is unchanged.

articles.title: Subject lookup after a dual-continuation update
articles.statement: The matched subject's rank is retained at its exact continuation.

articles.title: Dual advancement in the left part of a union
articles.statement:
A left parallel frame retains all its capabilities and the exact
subject head/rank/continuation correspondence of the actual update.

articles.title: Dual advancement in the right part of a disjoint union
articles.statement:
A right parallel frame requires the actual disjoint ownership split,
so its matched entries cannot be shadowed by the left-biased union.

articles.title: Head communication yields a dual advancement
articles.statement:
A typed opposite-head pair at an initially compatible interface yields
a faithful matched update and a compatible typed residual via the packed result.

articles.title: Head communication preserves typing and records the matched output
articles.statement:
For a typed opposite-head pair at an initially compatible interface,
the packed result retains the literal send head, payload kind and continuation
correspondence instead of hiding an unconstrained protocol.

articles.title: Dual advancement preserves the owned keys
articles.statement: Both matched old keys remain owned; the update creates no new key.

articles.title: A matched output head is a send with the same continuation
articles.statement: The detailed matched output determines the same literal continuation.

articles.title: Binder swapping preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Canonical swapping preserves full finite-process endpoint typing.

articles.title: Swapping nested restrictions exchanges their bound pairs
articles.statement:
Swapping nested restrictions exchanges their complete dual pairs and
fixes all lifted outer ownership, rather than forgetting any bound capability.

articles.title: Swapping the two innermost binders fixes a twice-lifted context
articles.statement: Two lifts put all outer names above both swapped binder indices.

articles.title: Context swapping commutes with insertion
articles.statement: Swapping maps an inserted capability to the swapped role key verbatim.

articles.title: Swapping two ambient binders in an ownership context
articles.statement: Swap ownership of two existing ambient binders without altering any role.

articles.title: Semantic advancement preserves balance
articles.statement:
From a semantically balanced initial interface, actual advancement retains
balance with exact old keys and actual new codes.

articles.title: The empty context is semantically balanced
articles.statement: Empty interface balance is not a completion assertion about private work.

articles.title: Raw balance implies semantic balance
articles.statement: Literal raw balance is a special case, not the semantic definition.

articles.title: Semantic balance of a linear context
articles.statement: Every actual owned key has a semantic dual peer at equal capability rank.

articles.title: Semantic advancement preserves compatibility
articles.statement: Actual compatible source retains semantic duality after the exact update.

articles.title: Semantic balance implies semantic compatibility
articles.statement: Semantic balance supplies semantic compatibility by actual lookup uniqueness.

articles.title: Semantic advancement preserves disjointness from a frame
articles.statement: No new key can conflict with a parallel ownership frame.

articles.title: Semantic advancement extends from the left part to the whole union
articles.statement: Left frame preserves actual old lookups and all literal head evidence.

articles.title: Semantic advancement extends from the right part to a disjoint union
articles.statement: Right frame uses actual disjointness so neither old subject is shadowed.

articles.title: Typed head communication yields a semantic advancement
articles.statement:
A typed opposite-head pair at an initially semantically compatible interface
yields a faithful semantic advance and a compatible typed residual.

articles.title: Lifting preserves semantic advancement
articles.statement: Canonical lifting preserves actual heads, ranks and code-valued payloads.

articles.title: Literally dual capabilities have literally dual continuations
articles.statement: Literal duality of the ORIGINAL codes forces literal tail equality.

articles.title: Semantic advancement preserves the context's domain
articles.statement: Exact domain preservation includes completed capabilities.

articles.title: Raw dual advancement is a semantic advancement
articles.statement: Raw actual dual-code advancement embeds into the semantic relation.

articles.title: Semantic advancement preserves capability ranks
articles.statement: Every actual capability retains its enclosing rank at the same key.

articles.title: Semantic advancement preserves scoping of owned keys
articles.statement: Canonical scope of the whole owned domain is preserved.

articles.title: Semantic advancement of a communicating endpoint pair
articles.statement:
Actual old sender/peer values and literal continuations, not raw dual-code
identity. Target is EXACTLY the two actual subject insertions.

articles.title: Communication heads give a send-head observation
articles.statement: The existing raw send-head observation is reused only as a pure head fact.

articles.title: Binder swapping preserves semantic advancement
articles.statement: Canonical swapping permutes only subject keys, never the protocol codes.

articles.title: Semantic advancement is raw under literal compatibility
articles.statement:
Reverse bridge requires literal ORIGINAL peer compatibility, not merely
semantic compatibility or residual retyping.

articles.title: Outer insertion commutes with binding a fresh pair
articles.statement: Installing an outer capability commutes with the entire fresh bound pair.

articles.title: Outer dual advancement lifts through restriction
articles.statement:
An actual external matched update lifts through restriction without
altering its private pair, even when the payload protocol refers to private data.

articles.title: Lowering preserves disjointness of outer contexts
articles.statement: Lowering disjoint outer-only contexts preserves their exact key split.

articles.title: Erasing both roles of the fresh name leaves outer keys
articles.statement: Removing both roles of var zero leaves only genuine outer-name keys.

articles.title: Lowering is injective on contexts without fresh-name keys
articles.statement:
Canonical lowering is injective on an outer context with no fresh-name
role. The inverse is canonical lift, not a guessed fresh constant identity.

articles.title: Endpoint typing absorbs a role absent from its parallel partner
articles.statement:
A role missing from one component can be reattached only after actual
absence in its typed partner derives completion of the advertised capability.

articles.title: Lifting a lowered context recovers it
articles.statement: Lifting the recovered outer context restores every key and capability.

articles.title: Lowering then lifting an outer key returns it
articles.statement:
Canonical lowering and lifting cancel for a polarized outer key,
provided it is not either role of the freshly inserted physical name.

articles.title: Context lifting is injective
articles.statement: Canonical context lifting is injective, including recorded completed slots.

articles.title: Outer lookups pass through a freshly bound pair
articles.statement:
An outer lifted role lookup passes through both fresh bound entries
and reflects to the exact old external capability.

articles.title: Lowering of an outer context past a fresh binder
articles.statement: Remove a fresh ambient binder from a finite outer ownership context.

articles.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for restriction
articles.statement: Restriction inversion exposes the actual bound dual pair.

articles.title: Dual advancement under restriction splits, keeping the private step
articles.statement:
Projection additionally retains an actual private old-head/continuation
transition when the communication is hidden by ν. It does not reduce private
advancement to an arbitrary capability with the same rank.

articles.title: Dual advancement under restriction splits into inner and outer cases
articles.statement:
Exact pure restriction projection. An internal matched pair changes
only the bound pair at the same rank; an outer matched pair changes only the
external context and retains the entire old bound pair.

articles.title: Endpoint typing restores both bound roles to the restricted side
articles.statement:
In the actual scope split, either freshly bound role can be moved
back to the restricted component only when partner absence proves it completed.

articles.title: Endpoint typing is preserved by forward scope extrusion
articles.statement:
The forward canonical scope rule preserves the exact external context
and ambient depth, with the dual pair derived from restriction typing.

articles.title: Endpoint typing is preserved by reverse scope extrusion
articles.statement:
Reverse scope transport recovers the exact external ownership split
from the actual restriction/parallel typing, with no closed-hole premise.

articles.title: Endpoint typing reflects through binder lifting
articles.statement:
Typing an actually lifted term under outer-only ownership reflects
back to its exact recovered context; no closed-hole premise is required.

articles.title: Updating both bound roles, negative first, rebinds the pair
articles.statement:
A negative sender installs the dual continuation on the positive role;
reordering the distinct insertions retains the same complete bound pair.

articles.title: Updating both bound roles, positive first, rebinds the pair
articles.statement:
Two updates at the fresh positive/negative roles replace only the
bound capability pair and retain the entire lifted external context.

articles.title: Binding a dual private pair preserves balance
articles.statement:
At a semantically balanced outer interface, binding an exact dual private
pair retains balance for the pair and every actual outer peer.

articles.title: Binding a fresh dual pair preserves dual compatibility
articles.statement: A fresh complete bound pair extends any ordinary compatible interface.

articles.title: Outer semantic advances lift past a private binding
articles.statement: An actual outer semantic advance lifts without changing its private pair.

articles.title: Binding a dual private pair preserves compatibility
articles.statement: A chosen exact dual private pair extends a semantically compatible interface.

articles.title: Structural congruence preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement:
Every existing canonical structural congruence preserves endpoint typing
in both directions with exactly the same depth and ownership. Unsupported
choice/replication shapes are rejected by the typing-derived finite invariant.

articles.title: Removing a restriction around nil preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Restriction of nil has exactly the completed external ownership of nil.

articles.title: Adding a restriction around nil preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement:
A completed fresh pair may be introduced around nil while retaining
all original external capabilities and scope.

articles.title: Reverse restriction swap preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Reverse nested restriction commutation uses the canonical involution.

articles.title: Swapping nested restrictions preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Nested restriction commutation swaps their derived complete dual pairs.

articles.title: Reverse parallel reassociation preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Reverse reassociation recovers both sub-splits from the supplied typing.

articles.title: Parallel reassociation preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Parallel reassociation preserves the actual three-way disjoint split.

articles.title: Parallel commutation preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Parallel commutation swaps a derived disjoint split, not its capabilities.

articles.title: Adding a parallel nil preserves endpoint typing
articles.statement: Adding a parallel nil allocates it no ownership; no active slot is dropped.

articles.title: Semantic advance under a private binding is private or outer
articles.statement:
Faithful projection retains an actual private-pair advance OR the actual
outer advance and unchanged bound pair. It never chooses an arbitrary Xi.

articles.title: Injective rekeying preserves dual compatibility
articles.statement: Injective physical-name rekeying retains partial dual compatibility.

articles.title: Equivalent retyping preserves semantic balance
articles.statement: Pointwise semantic recoding retains actual paired domain and cap ranks.

articles.title: Endpoint typing is invariant under scope extrusion
articles.statement:
Both directions of the canonical scope congruence preserve exact
external polarized ownership and the unchanged ambient binder depth.

articles.title: Compatibility restricts to the left part of a union
articles.statement: Left children inherit actual peer compatibility.

articles.title: Compatibility restricts to the right part of a disjoint union
articles.statement: A disjoint right child inherits actual peer compatibility without shadowing.

articles.title: Union of disjoint balanced contexts is balanced
articles.statement: Disjoint balanced components form a balanced ownership frame union.

articles.title: Subject reduction for endpoint typing at balanced interfaces
articles.statement:
A typed source with a balanced initial interface retains typing and balance
after any canonical step. Balance supplies the required compatibility; the
exact zero-or-one external advancement evidence is retained.

articles.title: Subject reduction for endpoint typing at the empty interface
articles.statement:
An empty-interface typed network retains empty-interface typing through
any canonical step. The empty context is balanced, hence compatible, including
communication behind restrictions and pre/post congruence.

articles.title: Subject reduction for endpoint typing at compatible interfaces
articles.statement:
From a typed source at an initially compatible interface, all five
canonical reduction constructors preserve typing and compatibility, with one
matched external subject-pair advancement or an unchanged interface when
communication is private. No fragment or enabled-edge premise is required.

articles.title: Assertion
articles.statement:
An assertion is a predicate on program states: it assigns a proposition to
each state. Assertions serve as the preconditions and postconditions of Hoare triples.

articles.title: Counted loop runs are big-step executions
articles.statement:
Let $b$ be a boolean expression, $c$ a
command, $n$ a natural number and $s$, $t$ states. If the loop
$\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in $t$ after exactly $n$
executions of the body $c$, then the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ runs from $s$
to $t$ in the big-step semantics.

articles.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic is relatively complete
articles.statement:
For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and
every command $c$, if the total-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is valid, then it is
derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic.

articles.title: Relative completeness of total-correctness Hoare logic
articles.statement:
For all assertions $P$ and $Q$
and every command $c$, if the total-correctness triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and
postcondition $Q$ is valid, then it is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the loop iteration count
articles.statement:
Let $b$ be a boolean expression, $c$ a command
and $s$ a state. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in
a state $t$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body and also exits in a state $t'$ after
exactly $m$ executions of the body, then $n = m$.

articles.title: Total-correctness derivations give partial-correctness derivations
articles.statement:
For all assertions
$P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, if the triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and
postcondition $Q$ is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic, then it is derivable in
partial-correctness Hoare logic.

articles.title: Partial-correctness Hoare logic matches the denotational semantics
articles.statement:
For all assertions
$P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, the partial-correctness triple with precondition $P$, command
$c$ and postcondition $Q$ is derivable if and only if, for all states $s$ and $t$ such that $P$
holds at $s$ and the pair $(s, t)$ lies in the relational denotation of $c$, $Q$ holds at $t$.

articles.title: Derivability in the default inference system on Hoare triples is validity
articles.statement:
For every
Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$, the triple is derivable in the default inference system on Hoare
triples, which is partial-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if it is valid for partial
correctness.

articles.title: Partial-correctness Hoare logic as an inference system
articles.statement:
A Hoare triple, given by a
precondition $P$, a command $c$ and a postcondition $Q$, is derivable in the default inference
system on Hoare triples, which is partial-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if it is valid
for partial correctness.

articles.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic as an inference system
articles.statement:
A Hoare triple, given by a
precondition $P$, a command $c$ and a postcondition $Q$, is derivable in the inference system on
Hoare triples tagged total correctness, which is total-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if
it is valid for total correctness.

articles.title: The weakest liberal precondition gives a derivable triple
articles.statement:
For every command $c$ and
every assertion $Q$, the triple whose precondition is the weakest liberal precondition of $c$
with respect to $Q$, whose command is $c$ and whose postcondition is $Q$ is derivable in
partial-correctness Hoare logic.

articles.title: Derivability in Hoare logic for partial correctness
articles.statement:
Here an assertion is a predicate on
states, and an assertion $P$ entails an assertion $P'$ when every state satisfying $P$ satisfies
$P'$. For an assertion $P$ and a Boolean expression $b$, the assertion $P \land b$ holds in a
state when $P$ holds there and $b$ evaluates to true in it, and the assertion $P \land \lnot b$
holds in a state when $P$ holds there and $b$ evaluates to false in it. Derivability of
partial-correctness Hoare triples $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is the least relation closed under the
following rules, where $P$, $P'$, $Q$, $Q'$, $R$ and $I$ are assertions, $c$, $c_1$ and $c_2$ are
commands, $x$ is a variable, $a$ is an arithmetic expression and $b$ is a Boolean expression.

* Skip: $\{Q\}\,\mathtt{skip}\,\{Q\}$.
* Assignment: $\{Q[a/x]\}\,x := a\,\{Q\}$, where $Q[a/x]$ holds in a state $s$ when $Q$ holds in
  the state obtained from $s$ by setting $x$ to the value of $a$ in $s$.
* Sequencing: from $\{P\}\,c_1\,\{R\}$ and $\{R\}\,c_2\,\{Q\}$ derive $\{P\}\,c_1; c_2\,\{Q\}$.
* Conditional: from $\{P \land b\}\,c_1\,\{Q\}$ and $\{P \land \lnot b\}\,c_2\,\{Q\}$ derive
  $\{P\}\,\mathtt{if}\ b\ \mathtt{then}\ c_1\ \mathtt{else}\ c_2\,\{Q\}$.
* While: from $\{I \land b\}\,c\,\{I\}$ derive
  $\{I\}\,\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c\,\{I \land \lnot b\}$.
* Consequence: if $P$ entails $P'$, $\{P'\}\,c\,\{Q'\}$ is derivable and $Q'$ entails $Q$, then
  $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable.

articles.title: Entailment of assertions
articles.statement:
An assertion $P$ entails an assertion $Q$ when every state
that satisfies $P$ also satisfies $Q$.

articles.title: Every terminating loop run has an iteration count
articles.statement:
Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a
command and $s$, $s'$ states. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ has a terminating
big-step execution from $s$ to $s'$, then there is a natural number $n$ such that the loop,
started in $s$, exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$.

articles.title: Loop invariants entail the weakest liberal precondition of the loop
articles.statement:
Let $I$ and $Q$
be assertions, $b$ a Boolean expression and $c$ a command. Suppose that every state satisfying
$I$ in which $b$ evaluates to true satisfies the weakest liberal precondition of $c$ with
