articles.title: Fundamental lemma for NbE evaluation
articles.statement:
Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types.
Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, let $\xi$ be a Kripke semantic environment
assigning to each variable of $\Gamma$ a semantic value in context $\Delta$, and let $\eta$ and
$\theta$ be environments in $I$ for $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$. If $\xi$ realizes $\eta$ at $\theta$,
then the NbE evaluation of $t$ in $\xi$ realizes the denotation of $t$ in $\eta$ at $\theta$.

articles.title: Evaluation into the Kripke semantic domain
articles.statement:
Let $t$ be a term of type $T$ in context
$\Gamma$ and let $\eta$ be a semantic environment interpreting every variable of $\Gamma$ as a
semantic value in context $\Delta$. The evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(t, \eta)$ is the semantic
value of type $T$ in context $\Delta$ defined by recursion on $t$: a variable $x$ evaluates to
$\eta(x)$; an application $f\,a$ evaluates to the semantic function $\operatorname{ev}(f, \eta)$
applied, along the identity renaming of $\Delta$, to $\operatorname{ev}(a, \eta)$; and an
abstraction $\lambda b$ of type $A \to B$, whose body $b$ lies in the context $\Gamma$ extended
by $A$, evaluates to the semantic function that sends a renaming $\rho$ from $\Delta$ to a context
$\Theta$ and a semantic value $a$ of type $A$ in $\Theta$ to $\operatorname{ev}(b, \eta')$, where
$\eta'$ sends the new variable to $a$ and each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(x)$ renamed along
$\rho$.

articles.title: Kripke realization relation for NbE
articles.statement:
Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. For a
context $\Gamma$, an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$, a type $A$, a Kripke semantic value
$v$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ and an element $d$ of the denotation of $A$ under $I$, the relation
"$v$ realizes $d$ at $\eta$" is defined by recursion on $A$. At a base type, $v$ is a neutral
term, and $v$ realizes $d$ when the denotation of $v$, read as a term, in $\eta$ equals $d$. At a
function type $A \Rightarrow B$, $v$ realizes $d$ when for every context $\Delta$, every renaming
$\rho : \Gamma \to \Delta$, every environment $\theta$ for $\Delta$ with $\theta \circ \rho = \eta$,
every semantic value $a$ of type $A$ in $\Delta$ and every element $e$ of the denotation of $A$
such that $a$ realizes $e$ at $\theta$, the semantic value $v(\rho, a)$ realizes $d(e)$ at
$\theta$.

articles.title: Normal forms are fixed points of normalization
articles.statement:
For every beta-normal, eta-long normal
form $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of $n$ by evaluation
returns the normal form $n$ itself.

articles.title: Normalization by evaluation
articles.statement:
For a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, its normal
form is the beta-normal, eta-long term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ obtained by reifying, at
type $A$, the evaluation of $t$ in the identity semantic environment of $\Gamma$, which interprets
each variable as the reflection of that variable.

articles.title: NbE preserves denotation
articles.statement:
For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$
of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$, the NbE normal
form of $t$ has the same denotation in $\eta$ as $t$.

articles.title: Normalization by evaluation is idempotent
articles.statement:
For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context
$\Gamma$, normalizing the normalized term of $t$ by evaluation gives the normalized term of $t$
again.

articles.title: Every term is model-equal to its NbE normal form
articles.statement:
Every term $t$ of type $A$ in context
$\Gamma$ is model-equal to its NbE normal form.

articles.title: Renormalizing a computed normal form
articles.statement:
For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context
$\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of the normal form that normalization by evaluation
computes from $t$ gives the same term as normalizing $t$.

articles.title: Every term is semantically equal to its NbE normal form in each model
articles.statement:
For every
interpretation $I$ of the base types and every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, $t$ and
its NbE normal form are semantically equal in $I$: they have the same denotation in every
environment for $\Gamma$ in $I$.

articles.title: Normalization fixes the terms of normal forms
articles.statement:
For every eta-long normal form $n$ of
type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of $n$ returns that term
unchanged.

articles.title: Normalization of terms
articles.statement:
For a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, its normalized term
is the term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ underlying the beta-normal, eta-long normal form of $t$
computed by normalization by evaluation.

articles.title: Reflection commutes with renaming
articles.statement:
For every type $A$, every renaming $\rho$ from a
context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, and every neutral term $n$ of type $A$ in context
$\Gamma$, transporting the semantic value obtained by reflecting $n$ at type $A$ along $\rho$
gives the reflection at type $A$ of the neutral term $n$ renamed by $\rho$.

articles.title: Renaming a semantic environment
articles.statement:
Given a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Delta$ to a
context $\Theta$ and a semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$, the renamed
environment is the semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Theta$ that sends each variable $x$ of
type $A$ to the semantic value $\eta(x)$ renamed along $\rho$ at type $A$.

articles.title: Renaming preserves canonical terms
articles.statement:
If a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is
canonical, then for every renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the term
obtained by renaming $t$ along $\rho$ is canonical.

articles.title: Realization is stable under renaming
articles.statement:
Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. Let
$v$ be a Kripke semantic value of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ that realizes an element $d$ of
the denotation of $A$ at an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$. If $\rho : \Gamma \to \Delta$ is a
renaming and $\theta$ is an environment for $\Delta$ with $\theta \circ \rho = \eta$, then the
transport of $v$ along $\rho$ realizes $d$ at $\theta$.

articles.title: Renaming a semantic value
articles.statement:
Given a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context
$\Delta$, a simple type $A$ and a semantic value $v$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the renamed value is
the semantic value of type $A$ in $\Delta$ defined by cases on $A$. At a base type it is the
neutral term $v$ with its free variables renamed by $\rho$. At an arrow type
$A = B \Rightarrow C$ it sends a renaming $\sigma$ from $\Delta$ to a context $\Theta$ and a
semantic value $a$ of type $B$ in $\Theta$ to the semantic value of type $C$ in $\Theta$ that $v$
assigns to the composite renaming ($\rho$ followed by $\sigma$) and $a$.

articles.title: Semantic environments for normalization by evaluation
articles.statement:
For contexts $\Delta$ and
$\Gamma$, a semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$ assigns to every variable of $\Gamma$,
of any type $A$, a Kripke semantic value of type $A$ in $\Delta$.

articles.title: Kripke semantic values
articles.statement:
For a context $\Gamma$, the semantic values of a simple type in
$\Gamma$ are defined by recursion on the type. At a base type $b$ they are the neutral terms of
type $b$ in $\Gamma$ (variables applied to zero or more normal arguments). At an arrow type
$A \Rightarrow B$ a semantic value is a family that, for every context $\Delta$ and every
renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, maps semantic values of type $A$ in $\Delta$ to semantic
values of type $B$ in $\Delta$.

Because a semantic function acts after every renaming into a later context, reification under a
binder needs no untyped weakening operation.

articles.title: Normal forms as canonical terms
articles.statement:
The canonical term of an eta-long normal form $n$ of
type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the underlying term of $n$, certified to be a fixed point of
normalization.

articles.title: The normal form of a canonical term
articles.statement:
For a canonical term $t$ of type $A$ in context
$\Gamma$, that is, a term that normalization returns unchanged, its normal form is the
eta-long normal form that normalization by evaluation computes from $t$.

articles.title: Erasing normal forms is injective
articles.statement:
For every context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, two
eta-long normal forms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ with the same underlying term are equal.

NbE gives an explicit left inverse, so no separate syntactic injectivity argument is
needed.

articles.title: Reducibility is closed under backward evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of
the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps and $t'$ is
reducible, then $t$ is reducible.

articles.title: Left expansion preserves having the same result
articles.statement:
Let $t$, $t'$ and $u$ be closed terms of
the same type. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, and $t'$ and $u$ have
the same result, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.

articles.title: Right expansion preserves having the same result
articles.statement:
Let $t$, $u$ and $u'$ be closed terms
of the same type. If $u$ reduces to $u'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, and $t$ and $u'$
have the same result, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.

articles.title: Termination is closed under backward evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of
the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps and $t'$
terminates, then $t$ terminates.

articles.title: Evaluating the argument of a value function is a multi-step congruence
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a term
of type $A \Rightarrow B$ and let $a$, $a'$ be terms of type $A$, all in the same context. If $f$
is a value and $a$ evaluates to $a'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then the application
$f\,a$ evaluates to $f\,a'$ in zero or more steps.

articles.title: Multi-step evaluation is a congruence in function position
articles.statement:
Let $f$ and $f'$ be terms
of type $A \Rightarrow B$ and let $a$ be a term of type $A$, all in the same context. If $f$
evaluates to $f'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then the application $f\,a$ evaluates
to $f'\,a$ in zero or more steps.

articles.title: Application preserves having the same result
articles.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be closed terms of a
function type $A \Rightarrow B$, and let $a$ and $b$ be closed terms of type $A$. If $f$ and $g$
have the same result and $a$ and $b$ have the same result, then the applications $f\,a$ and
$g\,b$ have the same result.

articles.title: Closed functions evaluate to lambda abstractions
articles.statement:
For every closed term $f$ of a function
type $A \Rightarrow B$ there is a term $b$ of type $B$ in the context with a single variable of
type $A$ such that $f$ reduces, in zero or more call-by-value steps, to the lambda abstraction
with body $b$.

articles.title: Extending a reducible substitution by a reducible term keeps it reducible
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$
be a substitution that sends each variable of a context $\Gamma$ to a closed term of the same
type, and let $a$ be a closed term of type $A$. If $\sigma$ and $a$ are reducible, then so is
the substitution on the context $A, \Gamma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each
older variable $x$ to $\sigma(x)$.

articles.title: Substitutions on the empty context are reducible
articles.statement:
Every substitution from the empty
context to closed terms is reducible, since the empty context has no variables.

articles.title: Values reduce only to themselves
articles.statement:
Let $v$ and $t$ be terms of the same type in the same
context. If $v$ is a value and $v$ reduces to $t$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then
$v = t$.

articles.title: Reducibility is closed under forward evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of
the same type. If $t$ is reducible and $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value
steps, then $t'$ is reducible.

articles.title: Termination is closed under forward evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of
the same type. If $t$ terminates and $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value
steps, then $t'$ terminates.

articles.title: Fundamental theorem of the reducibility relation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in a
context $\Gamma$, and let $\sigma$ be a reducible substitution sending each variable of $\Gamma$
to a closed term of the same type. Then the closed term obtained by applying $\sigma$ to $t$ is
reducible.

The lambda case is the key: evaluate an arbitrary reducible
argument to a value, cross the beta step, and invoke the induction hypothesis
under the extended substitution.

articles.title: Reducibility is invariant under evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the
same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t$ is reducible
if and only if $t'$ is reducible.

articles.title: Normalization and termination coincide
articles.statement:
A closed well-typed term $t$ normalizes, that is,
reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form (a term with no further reduction
step), if and only if it terminates, that is, reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a
value.

articles.title: No closed terms of base type
articles.statement:
In the pure, constant-free calculus there is no closed
term whose type is a base type.

articles.title: Uniqueness of normal forms
articles.statement:
If a closed term $t$ reduces in zero or more call-by-value
steps to a normal form $n$ and also to a normal form $m$, then $n = m$.

articles.title: Normalization of closed terms
articles.statement:
Every closed well-typed term normalizes: it reduces in
zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form.

articles.title: Normalizing closed terms
articles.statement:
A closed term $t$ of the simply typed lambda calculus normalizes
when it reduces, in zero or more call-by-value steps, to a term in normal form, that is, a term
with no further call-by-value reduction step.

articles.title: Evaluation preserves the result of a closed term
articles.statement:
If a closed term $t$ reduces to a
term $u$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.

articles.title: Values terminate
articles.statement:
Every closed term of the simply typed lambda calculus that is a value
terminates.

No evaluation step is needed: the value itself is the value reached.

articles.title: Closed terms are reducible
articles.statement:
Every closed well-typed term of the simply typed lambda
calculus is reducible.

articles.title: Reducible substitutions
articles.statement:
A substitution $\sigma$ that replaces each variable of a
context $\Gamma$ by a closed term of the same type is reducible when $\sigma(x)$ is reducible
for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$.

articles.title: Tait reducibility for closed terms
articles.statement:
Reducibility of a closed term $t$ is defined by
recursion on its simple type. At a base type, $t$ is reducible when it terminates. At a function
type $A \Rightarrow B$, $t$ is reducible when it terminates and, for every reducible closed term
$a$ of type $A$, the application $t\,a$ is reducible.

articles.title: Reflexivity of having the same result
articles.statement:
Every closed term has the same result as
itself.

articles.title: Having the same result is an equivalence relation
articles.statement:
For every simple type $A$, the
relation of having the same result is an equivalence relation on the closed terms of type $A$.

articles.title: Closed terms with the same result
articles.statement:
Two closed terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type have the
same result when there is a value $v$ such that both $t$ and $u$ reduce to $v$ in zero or more
call-by-value steps.

articles.title: Evaluation to a value passes through every reduct
articles.statement:
Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be terms of the
same type in the same context, with $v$ a value. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ and $t$ evaluates to
$t'$, each in finitely many call-by-value steps, then $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in finitely many
steps.

The value endpoint makes the first evaluation maximal, so every other finite
evaluation is one of its prefixes.

articles.title: Symmetry of having the same result
articles.statement:
If closed terms $t$ and $u$ have the same result,
then $u$ and $t$ have the same result.

articles.title: Reducible terms terminate
articles.statement:
Every reducible closed term of the simply typed lambda
calculus terminates.

articles.title: Termination of the call-by-value simply typed lambda calculus
articles.statement:
Every closed well-typed
term evaluates, in finitely many call-by-value steps, to a value.

articles.title: Termination of closed terms
articles.statement:
A closed term $t$ terminates when it evaluates, in
finitely many call-by-value steps, to a value.

articles.title: Transitivity of having the same result
articles.statement:
If closed terms $t$ and $u$ have the same result,
and $u$ and a closed term $v$ have the same result, then $t$ and $v$ have the same result.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the value reached by evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ be a term in any context. If $t$
reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a value $v$ and also to a value $w$, then
$v = w$.

articles.title: Big-step evaluation is closed under backward reduction steps
articles.statement:
Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be
terms of the same type $A$ in the same typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one
left-to-right call-by-value step and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written
$t' \Downarrow v$, then $t \Downarrow v$.

articles.title: Big-step evaluation is closed under backward multi-step reduction
articles.statement:
Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$
be terms of the same type $A$ in the same typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in
finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the
big-step semantics, written $t' \Downarrow v$, then $t \Downarrow v$.

articles.title: Canonical forms for closed function values
articles.statement:
If a term $f$ of function type
$A \Rightarrow B$ in the empty context is a value, then $f$ is a lambda abstraction: there is a
term $b$ of type $B$ in the one-variable context $[A]$ such that $f$ is the abstraction of $b$.

articles.title: Closed normal forms are exactly the values
articles.statement:
A term $t$ of type $A$ in the empty context
is in normal form, that is, has no call-by-value reduction step, if and only if it is a value.

articles.title: Small-step call-by-value reduction in STLC is deterministic
articles.statement:
For terms $t$, $t_1$,
$t_2$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, if $t$ reduces in one call-by-value step both to $t_1$
and to $t_2$, then $t_1 = t_2$.

articles.title: Determinism of big-step evaluation in the simply typed lambda calculus
articles.statement:
For every typing
context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, if a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ evaluates in the
big-step call-by-value semantics both to $v$ and to $w$, written $t \Downarrow v$ and
$t \Downarrow w$, then $v = w$.

articles.title: Big-step call-by-value evaluation in the simply typed lambda calculus
articles.statement:
Fix a typing
context $\Gamma$. For terms $t$ and $v$ of the same type in context $\Gamma$, the big-step
evaluation relation $t \Downarrow v$ is the least relation such that every lambda abstraction
$\lambda.\,b$ evaluates to itself, and an application $f\,a$ evaluates to $v$ whenever
$f \Downarrow \lambda.\,b$, $a \Downarrow u$ and $b[u] \Downarrow v$, where $b[u]$ is the body $b$
with its newest free variable replaced by $u$.

The application rule fixes a left-to-right order: first the function, then the argument, then
the instantiated body.

articles.title: Closed simply typed terms have a big-step evaluation
articles.statement:
For every type $A$ and every closed
term $t$ of type $A$, that is, a term in the empty typing context, there is a term $v$ such that
$t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-value semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.

articles.title: Big-step evaluation is small-step evaluation to a value
articles.statement:
For terms $t$ and $v$ of the
same type in the same typing context, $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written
$t \Downarrow v$, if and only if $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero)
left-to-right call-by-value steps and $v$ is a value, that is, a lambda abstraction.

articles.title: Normal forms for call-by-value reduction in STLC
articles.statement:
A term $t$ of type $A$ in a context
$\Gamma$ is in normal form when there is no term $t'$ such that $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one
call-by-value step.

articles.title: Small-step evaluation to a value implies big-step evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ and $v$ be terms of
the same type in the same typing context. If $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero)
left-to-right call-by-value steps and $v$ is a value, then $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step
semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.

articles.title: Progress for closed STLC terms
articles.statement:
Every term $t$ of type $A$ in the empty context is
either a value or reduces in one call-by-value step to some term $t'$.

articles.title: Small-step call-by-value reduction in STLC
articles.statement:
One-step reduction on terms of type $A$ in a
context $\Gamma$ is the least relation closed under three left-to-right call-by-value rules: if
$f$ reduces to $f'$, then the application $f\,a$ reduces to $f'\,a$; if $f$ is a value and $a$
reduces to $a'$, then $f\,a$ reduces to $f\,a'$; and if $a$ is a value, then the application of
the abstraction of $b$ to $a$ reduces to $b[a]$, the result of substituting $a$ for the newest
free variable of $b$.

articles.title: Multi-step call-by-value reduction in STLC
articles.statement:
For terms of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$,
multi-step reduction is the reflexive transitive closure of one-step call-by-value reduction.

articles.title: Termination in terms of big-step evaluation
articles.statement:
For every closed term $t$ of type $A$, that
is, a term in the empty typing context, $t$ terminates (it reduces to a value in finitely many
left-to-right call-by-value steps) if and only if there is a term $v$ such that $t$ evaluates to
$v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.

articles.title: Big-step evaluation implies small-step evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $t$ and $v$ be terms of the same
type in the same typing context. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written
$t \Downarrow v$, then $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right
call-by-value steps.

articles.title: Values of STLC
articles.statement:
A term of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is a value exactly when it is a
lambda abstraction.

articles.title: Values are irreducible
articles.statement:
If a term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is a value, then
there is no term $t'$ to which $t$ reduces in one call-by-value step.

articles.title: Values evaluate to themselves
articles.statement:
Every value $v$, that is, every lambda abstraction, of any
type in any typing context evaluates to itself in the big-step semantics: $v \Downarrow v$.

articles.title: Big-step evaluation produces values
Composition of renamings of simply typed contexts
articles.statement:
For contexts $\Gamma$, $\Delta$ and
$\Xi$, a renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and a renaming $\sigma$ from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$,
the composite of $\rho$ followed by $\sigma$ is the renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends
each variable $x$ to $\sigma(\rho(x))$.

articles.title: Right identity law for composition of substitutions
articles.statement:
For every simultaneous substitution
$\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in
$\Gamma$, the composite of $\sigma$ followed by the identity substitution on $\Delta$ sends $x$ to
$\sigma(x)$.

articles.title: Composing a single substitution with a substitution
articles.statement:
Let $a$ be a term of type $A$ in a
context $\Gamma$ and $\sigma$ a substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, and write $a[\sigma]$ for
the result of applying $\sigma$ to $a$. The composite of the single substitution of $a$ for the
newest variable followed by $\sigma$ agrees, at every variable $x$ of the context $\Gamma$
extended by a newest variable of type $A$, with the extension of $\sigma$ that sends the newest
variable to $a[\sigma]$.

articles.title: Composition of simply typed substitutions
articles.statement:
For substitutions $\sigma$ from a context
$\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and $\tau$ from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$, the composite of $\sigma$ followed by
$\tau$ is the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the
term obtained by applying $\tau$ to $\sigma(x)$.

articles.title: Extension of a simply typed substitution
articles.statement:
Given a term $a$ of type $A$ in a context
$\Delta$ and a substitution $\sigma$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, the extension of $\sigma$ by $a$ is
the substitution from the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ to $\Delta$
that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(x)$.

articles.title: Identity renaming of a simply typed context
articles.statement:
For every context $\Gamma$, the identity
renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ sends each variable to itself.

articles.title: Identity substitution (simply typed lambda calculus)
articles.statement:
For a context $\Gamma$, the identity
substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ sends each variable of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of
that variable alone.

articles.title: Instantiation is substitution by an extended identity
articles.statement:
Let $b$ be a term of type $B$ in
the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and $a$ a term of type $A$ in
$\Gamma$. Instantiating the newest variable of $b$ by $a$ gives the same term as applying to $b$
the substitution that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable to itself, that
is, the extension of the identity substitution on $\Gamma$ by $a$.

articles.title: Instantiating a weakened term
articles.statement:
For terms $b$ of type $B$ and $a$ of type $A$ in a context
$\Gamma$, weakening $b$ to the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ and then
instantiating that newest variable by $a$ gives back $b$.

articles.title: Instantiating a binder body (simply typed lambda calculus)
articles.statement:
Write $A :: \Gamma$ for the
context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$. Given a term $t$ of type $B$ in
context $A :: \Gamma$ and a term $a$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the instantiation of $t$
with $a$ is the term of type $B$ in context $\Gamma$ obtained by applying to $t$ the
single-variable substitution for $a$, which replaces the newest variable by $a$ and leaves the
older variables unchanged.

articles.title: Lifting a renaming under a binder
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a renaming from a context $\Gamma$ to a
context $\Delta$ and let $A$ be a simple type, and write $A :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained
by prepending $A$ to $\Gamma$. The lift of $\rho$ is the renaming from $A :: \Gamma$ to
$A :: \Delta$ that sends the variable $0$ to $0$ and sends the successor of a variable $x$ of
$\Gamma$ to the successor of $\rho(x)$.

articles.title: Lifting followed by single substitution
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from $\Gamma$ to
$\Delta$ and $a$ a term of type $A$ in $\Delta$. The composite of the lift of $\sigma$ under a
binder of type $A$ followed by the single substitution of $a$ for the newest variable agrees, at
every variable $x$ of the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, with the
extension of $\sigma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable $y$ to
$\sigma(y)$.

articles.title: Lifting a substitution under a binder (simply typed lambda calculus)
articles.statement:
Write $A :: \Gamma$
for the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$. Given a substitution $\sigma$
from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and a type $A$, its lift is the substitution from
$A :: \Gamma$ to $A :: \Delta$ that sends the newest variable to the term consisting of the
newest variable alone, and sends the successor of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the weakening
of the term $\sigma(x)$ into the context $A :: \Delta$.

articles.title: Substitution induced by a renaming (simply typed lambda calculus)
articles.statement:
For contexts $\Gamma$
and $\Delta$ and a type-preserving renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, the induced
substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting
of the variable $\rho(x)$ alone.

articles.title: Renamings of simply typed contexts
articles.statement:
For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ (lists of simple
types), a renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ assigns to every simple type $A$ and every variable
of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ a variable of type $A$ in $\Delta$.

articles.title: Renaming a simply typed term
articles.statement:
For a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context
$\Delta$, the renaming $t[\rho]$ of a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the term of
type $A$ in context $\Delta$ defined by recursion on $t$: $x[\rho] = \rho(x)$ for a variable
$x$, $(f\,a)[\rho] = f[\rho]\,a[\rho]$ for an application, and
$(\lambda s)[\rho] = \lambda (s[\rho^{\uparrow}])$ for an abstraction, where $\rho^{\uparrow}$
is the lift of $\rho$ under one binder.

articles.title: Renaming commutes with instantiation
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$,
$b$ a term of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and $a$
a term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. Renaming by $\rho$ the instantiation of the newest variable of $b$
by $a$ gives the instantiation of the newest variable of $b'$ by $a'$, where $b'$ is $b$ renamed
by the lift of $\rho$ under the binder and $a'$ is $a$ renamed by $\rho$.

articles.title: Lifting commutes with renaming substitution images
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from
$\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and $\rho$ a renaming from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$. Lift $\sigma$ under a binder
of type $A$ and rename each of its images by the lift of $\rho$ under the same binder. At every
variable $x$ of the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, this gives the
same term as the lift under that binder of the substitution that renames each image of $\sigma$
by $\rho$.

articles.title: Renaming after substitution in the simply typed calculus
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a substitution
from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, $\rho$ a renaming from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$ and $t$ a term of type $A$ in
$\Gamma$. Renaming by $\rho$ the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ gives the result of applying
to $t$ the substitution that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(x)$ renamed by
$\rho$.

articles.title: Renaming commutes with weakening for intrinsically typed STLC terms
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a
renaming from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $t$ a term of type $A$
in context $\Gamma$, and $B$ a type. Weakening $t$ by a new newest variable of type $B$ and then
renaming by the lift of $\rho$ under that variable gives the same term as renaming $t$ by $\rho$
and then weakening by a new newest variable of type $B$.

articles.title: Renaming the images of a substitution
articles.statement:
Given a substitution $\sigma$ from the typing
context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$ and a renaming $\rho$ from $\Delta$ to the typing
context $\Xi$, the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ obtained by renaming images sends each
variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the renaming of the term $\sigma(x)$ by $\rho$.

articles.title: Single-variable substitution (simply typed lambda calculus)
articles.statement:
Write $A :: \Gamma$ for the
context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$. Given a term $a$ of type $A$ in
context $\Gamma$, the single-variable substitution for $a$ is the substitution from
$A :: \Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and sends the successor of each
variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of the variable $x$ alone.

articles.title: Simultaneous substitutions of simply typed contexts
articles.statement:
For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$
(lists of simple types), a substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ assigns to every simple type
$A$ and every variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Delta$.

articles.title: Substituting by an extended substitution, via lifting
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from
the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $s$ a term of type $B$ in the context
$\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and $a$ a term of type $A$ in context
$\Delta$. Applying to $s$ the extension of $\sigma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ gives the
same term as applying the lift of $\sigma$ to $s$ and then replacing the newest variable of the
result by $a$.

articles.title: Substitution commutes with instantiation for intrinsically typed STLC terms
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$
be a substitution from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $s$ a term of
type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and $a$ a term of type
$A$ in context $\Gamma$. Replacing the newest variable of $s$ by $a$ and then applying $\sigma$
gives the same term as applying the lift of $\sigma$ to $s$ and then replacing the newest variable
of the result by the term obtained by applying $\sigma$ to $a$.

articles.title: Lifted substitution commutes with weakening for intrinsically typed STLC terms
articles.statement:
Let
$\sigma$ be a substitution from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $t$ a
term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and $B$ a type. Weakening $t$ by a new newest variable of
type $B$ and then applying the lift of $\sigma$ under that variable gives the same term as
applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and then weakening by a new newest variable of type $B$.

articles.title: Renaming then substituting an intrinsically typed STLC term
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a renaming from
the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $\sigma$ a substitution from $\Delta$
to the typing context $\Xi$, and $t$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$. Renaming $t$ by
$\rho$ and then applying $\sigma$ gives the same term as applying to $t$ the substitution that
sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(\rho(x))$.

articles.title: Single substitution cancels weakening
articles.statement:
Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in the typing context
$\Gamma$ and $a$ a term of type $B$ in context $\Gamma$. Weakening $t$ by a new newest variable of
type $B$ and then applying the substitution that replaces the newest variable by $a$ and leaves
every older variable unchanged gives back $t$.

articles.title: Composition of substitutions for intrinsically typed STLC terms
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a
substitution from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $\tau$ a
substitution from $\Delta$ to the typing context $\Xi$, and $t$ a term of type $A$ in context
$\Gamma$. Applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and then applying $\tau$ gives the same term as applying to $t$
the composite substitution, which sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the result of applying
$\tau$ to $\sigma(x)$.

articles.title: Simultaneous substitution (simply typed lambda calculus)
articles.statement:
Given a substitution $\sigma$
from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the result $t[\sigma]$ of applying $\sigma$ to a
term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the term of type $A$ in context $\Delta$ defined by
recursion on $t$: $x[\sigma] = \sigma(x)$ for a variable $x$,
$(f\,a)[\sigma] = f[\sigma]\,a[\sigma]$ for an application, and
$(\lambda u)[\sigma] = \lambda\,(u[\sigma'])$ for an abstraction with body $u$, where
$\sigma'$ is the lift of $\sigma$ under the binder. Because variables are de Bruijn indices, this
substitution is capture-avoiding.

articles.title: Intrinsically typed terms of the simply typed lambda calculus
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ range over
simple types and $\Gamma$ over contexts (lists of simple types); write $A \Rightarrow B$ for the
function type from $A$ to $B$ and $A :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained by prepending $A$ to
$\Gamma$. The terms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ are generated by three rules: every variable
of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ is a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$; if $f$ is a term of type
$A \Rightarrow B$ and $a$ is a term of type $A$, both in context $\Gamma$, then the application
$f\,a$ is a term of type $B$ in context $\Gamma$; and if $t$ is a term of type $B$ in the context
$A :: \Gamma$, then the abstraction $\lambda t$ is a term of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in context
$\Gamma$.

articles.title: Simple types
articles.statement:
Given a type $B$ of base types, the simple types over $B$ are generated by
two rules: every base type $b \in B$ is a simple type, and for simple types $A$ and $C$ the
function type $A \Rightarrow C$ is a simple type.

articles.title: Typed de Bruijn variables of the simply typed lambda calculus
articles.statement:
For a context $\Gamma$ (a
list of simple types) and a simple type $A$, the variables of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ are generated
by two rules: the variable $0$ is a variable of type $A$ in the context $A :: \Gamma$ obtained
by prepending $A$ to $\Gamma$, and if $x$ is a variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, then for every
simple type $B$ the successor of $x$ is a variable of type $A$ in $B :: \Gamma$.

articles.title: Weakening a simply typed term
articles.statement:
For a term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ and a
simple type $B$, write $B :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained by prepending $B$ to $\Gamma$. The
weakening of $t$ is the term of type $A$ in the context $B :: \Gamma$ obtained by renaming $t$
along the renaming that sends each variable of $\Gamma$ to its successor in $B :: \Gamma$.

articles.title: Type checking for raw STLC terms
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. Given a
context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types), a raw term $r$ and a simple type $A$, the type checker
returns true exactly when type inference for $r$ in $\Gamma$ returns the type $A$, and false
otherwise.

articles.title: Checked terms
articles.statement:
For a context $\Gamma$ of simple types, a checked term in $\Gamma$ is a pair
$(A, t)$ of a simple type $A$ and an intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$.

A successful elaboration returns such a pair: the inferred type together with an intrinsic
term at that type.

articles.title: Closed raw terms
articles.statement:
A raw term $t$ is closed when its list of free indices at binder
depth $0$ is empty.

articles.title: Agreement of renamings is preserved by composition
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a typed renaming
from context $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, let $\sigma$ be a typed renaming from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$,
and let $r, s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $\rho$ agrees with $r$ and $\sigma$ agrees with
$s$, then the composite renaming that applies $\rho$ and then $\sigma$ agrees with
$s \circ r$.

articles.title: Completeness of elaboration
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. If a raw term $r$
has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ under the declarative typing judgment, then elaborating $r$ in
$\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$ together with some intrinsically typed term of type
$A$ in $\Gamma$.

articles.title: Elaboration inverts erasure
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every
intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, elaborating the erasure of $t$ in
$\Gamma$ succeeds and returns exactly the pair $(A, t)$. In other words, erasure is a section of
elaboration.

articles.title: Elaboration preserves the input syntax
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. If
elaborating a raw term $r$ in context $\Gamma$ succeeds with type $A$ and intrinsically typed
term $t$, then the erasure of $t$ is exactly $r$.

articles.title: Soundness of elaboration
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. If elaborating a raw
term $r$ in context $\Gamma$ succeeds with type $A$ (and some intrinsically typed term of type $A$
in $\Gamma$), then $r$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ under the declarative typing judgment.

articles.title: Elaboration of raw STLC terms
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. Elaboration in
a context $\Gamma$ of simple types sends a raw term either to failure or to a checked term in
$\Gamma$ (a simple type together with an intrinsically typed term of that type in $\Gamma$), by
recursion on the raw term. A variable with de Bruijn index $n$ elaborates to the variable at
position $n$ of $\Gamma$ (counting from $0$ at the front), with the type stored there, and fails
if $\Gamma$ has at most $n$ entries. A lambda with parameter type $A$ and body $b$ elaborates $b$
in $\Gamma$ extended by $A$ at the front; if that gives type $B$, it returns the lambda at type
$A \to B$, and otherwise it fails. An application of $f$ to $a$ elaborates $f$ and $a$ in
$\Gamma$, and succeeds, returning the application at type $B$, exactly when $f$ gets a function
type $A \to B$ and $a$ gets type $A$; otherwise it fails.

articles.title: Erasure preserves typing
articles.statement:
For every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context
$\Gamma$, the erasure of $t$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ under the declarative typing judgment for
raw terms.

articles.title: Erasure is injective
articles.statement:
For a fixed context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, erasure is injective on
intrinsically typed terms of type $A$ in $\Gamma$: two such terms with the same erasure are
equal.

articles.title: Erasure commutes with renaming
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a typed renaming from context $\Gamma$
to $\Delta$ and let $r : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a numerical renaming that agrees with
$\rho$. Then for every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the
erasure of the renamed term $\rho(t)$ equals the raw renaming by $r$ (lifted at every binder)
of the erasure of $t$.

articles.title: Erasure of a weakened term
articles.statement:
For every intrinsically typed term $t$ in context $\Gamma$
and every type $B$, the erasure of the weakening of $t$ to the context $\Gamma$ extended by
$B$ equals the raw renaming by the successor map $n \mapsto n + 1$ (lifted at every binder)
of the erasure of $t$. Thus every free index is incremented by one.

articles.title: Erasure of intrinsically typed terms
articles.statement:
The erasure of an intrinsically typed term in a
context $\Gamma$ is the raw term defined by recursion: a variable becomes the raw variable whose
index is its position in $\Gamma$ (counting from $0$ at the front); an application of $f$ to $a$
becomes the raw application of the erasure of $f$ to the erasure of $a$; and a lambda with
parameter type $B$ becomes the raw lambda annotated with $B$ whose body is the erasure of its
body. Erasure thus forgets all typing information except the binder annotations.

articles.title: Free indices of a raw term
articles.statement:
For a binder depth $d$ and a raw term $t$, the free
indices of $t$ at depth $d$ form a list defined by recursion on $t$: a variable with index $n$
contributes $[n - d]$ if $d \le n$ and the empty list otherwise; an application contributes
the free indices of the function followed by those of the argument, both at depth $d$; and a
lambda abstraction contributes the free indices of its body at depth $d + 1$.

articles.title: Declarative typing of raw terms
articles.statement:
For a context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types), a
raw term $t$ and a type $A$, the judgment $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ is the least relation closed
under three rules. A variable with de Bruijn index $n$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ whenever looking
up $n$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with the type $A$ and some intrinsic variable of type $A$. If
$\Gamma \vdash f : A \Rightarrow B$ and $\Gamma \vdash a : A$, then the application $f\,a$ has
type $B$ in $\Gamma$. If $A :: \Gamma \vdash b : B$, where $A :: \Gamma$ is $\Gamma$ with $A$
added at the front, then the abstraction $\lambda{:}A.\,b$ with parameter type $A$ has type
$A \Rightarrow B$ in $\Gamma$.

articles.title: Declarative typing agrees with elaboration
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable.
For every context $\Gamma$, raw term $t$ and type $A$, the declarative typing judgment
$\Gamma \vdash t : A$ holds if and only if there is an intrinsically typed term $u$ of type $A$
in context $\Gamma$ such that elaborating $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$
together with $u$.

articles.title: Indices occurring in a raw term
articles.statement:
The list of de Bruijn indices of a raw term, read
from left to right with repetitions: a variable with index $n$ gives $[n]$, an application
gives the indices of the function followed by those of the argument, and a lambda abstraction
gives the indices of its body, unshifted.

Bound occurrences are intentionally included, so this list is useful for diagnostics rather
than for scoping.

articles.title: Type inference is sound and complete
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. For
every context $\Gamma$, raw term $t$ and type $A$, type inference for $t$ in $\Gamma$ returns
$A$ if and only if the declarative typing judgment $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ holds.

articles.title: Type inference for raw terms
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. Given a
context $\Gamma$ and a raw term $t$, type inference elaborates $t$ in $\Gamma$; if elaboration
succeeds, it returns the type component of the result and forgets the intrinsically typed term,
and if elaboration fails, inference fails.

articles.title: Lifting commutes with composition of numerical renamings
articles.statement:
For maps
$\rho, \sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the lift of $\sigma \circ \rho$ through one binder
equals the lift of $\sigma$ composed after the lift of $\rho$.

articles.title: Lifting a numerical renaming
articles.statement:
Given a renaming $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of
de Bruijn indices, its lift through one binder is the map $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ sending
$0$ to $0$ and $n + 1$ to $\rho(n) + 1$.

articles.title: Agreement of renamings is preserved by lifting
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a typed renaming from
context $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and let $r : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a numerical renaming
that agrees with $\rho$. Then for every type $A$, the lift of $\rho$ under a binder of type
$A$ agrees with the lift of $r$ through one binder.

articles.title: Lookup returns a variable with the queried index
articles.statement:
For every context $\Gamma$ and
natural number $n$, if looking up the de Bruijn index $n$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with a type $A$
and an intrinsic variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, then the de Bruijn index of $x$ is $n$.

articles.title: Lookup recovers an intrinsic variable from its index
articles.statement:
For every context $\Gamma$, type
$A$ and intrinsic variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, looking up the de Bruijn index of $x$ in
$\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$ together with $x$.

articles.title: Variable lookup
articles.statement:
Given a context $\Gamma$, a list of types, and a natural number $n$,
looking up the de Bruijn index $n$ in $\Gamma$ either fails or returns a type $A$ together with
an intrinsic variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. It is defined by recursion: lookup fails in the
empty context; index $0$ in the context $A :: \Gamma$, obtained by adding $A$ at the front of
$\Gamma$, returns $A$ with the zero variable; and index $n + 1$ in $B :: \Gamma$ looks up $n$ in
$\Gamma$, fails if that fails, and otherwise returns the same type with the successor of the
variable found.

articles.title: Raw normalization of an erased term
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. For
every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, raw normalization of the
erasure of $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns the type $A$ together with the erasure of the
normal form of $t$ computed by normalization by evaluation.

articles.title: Raw normalization produces well-typed terms
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is
decidable. For every context $\Gamma$ and raw term $t$, if raw normalization of $t$ in $\Gamma$
succeeds with a type $A$ and a raw term $t'$, then the declarative typing judgment
$\Gamma \vdash t' : A$ holds.

articles.title: Raw normalization is idempotent
articles.statement:
Assume equality of base types is decidable. For every
context $\Gamma$ and raw term $t$, if raw normalization of $t$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with a type
$A$ and a raw term $t'$, then raw normalization of $t'$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds with the same type
$A$ and the same term $t'$.

articles.title: Raw normalization reports the inferred type
articles.statement:
Let the base types have decidable
equality, let $\Gamma$ be a context of simple types and let $r$ be a raw term. If normalizing
$r$ in $\Gamma$ succeeds and returns a type $A$ together with a raw term, then type inference
for $r$ in $\Gamma$ returns $A$.

articles.title: Normalization of raw terms
articles.statement:
Let the base types have decidable equality. Given a context
$\Gamma$ of simple types and a raw term $r$, raw normalization elaborates $r$ in $\Gamma$. If
elaboration fails, raw normalization fails. If elaboration returns a type $A$ and an
intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$, raw normalization returns $A$ together with the
erasure to a raw term of the normal form of $t$ computed by normalization by evaluation.

articles.title: Raw lambda terms
articles.statement:
Raw terms are extrinsic de Bruijn syntax over a given type of base
types: a raw term is either a variable given by a natural-number index $n$, an application
$f\,a$ of two raw terms $f$ and $a$, or a lambda abstraction $\lambda A.\,t$ consisting of a
simple type $A$ over the base types (the parameter type) and a raw term $t$ (the body).
Variables and applications carry no type information.

articles.title: Agreement of a typed and a numerical renaming
articles.statement:
A typed renaming $\rho$ from context
$\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$ agrees with a map $r : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ when, for every
type $A$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the de Bruijn index of $\rho(x)$
equals $r$ applied to the de Bruijn index of $x$.

articles.title: Composition of renamings of raw terms
articles.statement:
For all maps
$\rho, \sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every raw term $t$, renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then
renaming the result by $\sigma$ gives the same raw term as renaming $t$ by the composite
$\sigma \circ \rho$.

articles.title: Agreeing numerical renamings coincide on erased terms
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a type-preserving
renaming of variables from context $\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$, and let
$r, s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ both agree with $\rho$: for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, the
de Bruijn index of $\rho(x)$ is the image of the index of $x$ under $r$, and also under $s$. Then
for every intrinsically typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, renaming the erasure of $t$
by $r$ and renaming it by $s$ give the same raw term.

articles.title: Renaming of raw terms
articles.statement:
Given a map $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ on de Bruijn indices,
renaming a raw term by $\rho$ replaces each variable $n$ by $\rho(n)$, renames both parts of an
application by $\rho$, and renames the body of a lambda abstraction, keeping its parameter type,
by the lifted map $\rho'$ given by $\rho'(0) = 0$ and $\rho'(n + 1) = \rho(n) + 1$.

articles.title: Shifting raw terms
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ (the amount) and $c$ (the cutoff, $0$ by
default), shifting a raw term by $k$ at cutoff $c$ replaces a variable index $n$ by $n + k$ if
$c \le n$ and leaves it unchanged otherwise, shifts both sides of an application by $k$ at
cutoff $c$, and sends $\lambda A.\,t$ to $\lambda A.\,t'$, where $t'$ is $t$ shifted by $k$ at
cutoff $c + 1$.

articles.title: Renaming preserves the size of a raw term
articles.statement:
For every map $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
and every raw term $t$, the renaming of $t$ by $\rho$ has the same number of syntax nodes as $t$.

articles.title: Shifting preserves the size of a raw term
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $k$ and $c$ and every
raw term $t$, shifting $t$ by $k$ at cutoff $c$ (adding $k$ to each variable index that is at
least the cutoff, which grows by one under each binder) gives a raw term with the same number
of syntax nodes as $t$.

articles.title: Size of a raw term
articles.statement:
Writing $|t|$ for the size of a raw term $t$, the size counts the
syntax nodes of $t$: a variable has size $1$, an application $f\,a$ has size $|f| + |a| + 1$,
and a lambda abstraction $\lambda A.\,t$ has size $|t| + 1$, so the type annotation $A$ is
not counted.

articles.title: Index of a typed variable
articles.statement:
For a context $\Gamma$ and a type $A$, a well-typed de Bruijn
variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ is sent to its natural-number index, forgetting its type: the
variable for the first entry of the context has index $0$, and the successor of a variable $x$
has the index of $x$ plus $1$.

articles.title: Uniqueness of types for raw terms
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a context of simple types and $r$ a
raw term. If $r$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$ and $r$ has type $B$ in $\Gamma$ under the declarative
typing judgment for raw terms, then $A = B$.
